exercises.name: 90/90 Hip Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Seated on the floor with one leg bent 90 degrees in front (shin parallel to shoulders, knee pointing outward) and the other leg bent 90 degrees behind (shin pointing backward). Torso upright, hands on the floor for light support. Hips open, gentle forward lean over the front shin.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is seated with their torso folded forward over the front leg, chest approaching or touching the front shin while maintaining the 90/90 leg configuration (front shin parallel to shoulders with knee splayed outward, back shin pointing straight back). The spine is rounded in flexion, shoulders are internally rotated and drawn forward, and the hamstrings, glutes, and hip external rotators of the front leg appear fully engaged and stretched. The person's gaze is directed downward toward the front knee.

exercises.name: Abdominal Bracing
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor. The abdominal muscles are contracted as if bracing for a punch to the stomach, creating a rigid cylinder around the midsection. The spine maintains its natural curve, the ribs do not flare, and breathing continues normally while the brace is held.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains supine on their back with knees bent at approximately 90 degrees and feet flat on the floor, while the abdominal wall appears deeply indented and rigidly contracted, creating a visible hollowed appearance across the entire midsection from sternum to pelvis. The torso maintains a neutral spine position with no arching or flaring of the ribs, and the rectus abdominis, transverse abdominis, and obliques all appear maximally engaged and tensioned like a tight corset around the core.

exercises.name: Ankle Alphabet
exercises.pose_description: Standing on one leg or seated with one leg crossed over the other. The foot of the elevated leg traces the letters of the alphabet in the air using ankle movements only, moving through all planes of motion. The lower leg remains still while the foot moves deliberately through each letter shape.
exercises.end_pose_description: The standing leg is slightly bent at the knee with the hip engaged, while the elevated leg is extended with the foot positioned at the furthest point of completing a letter (typically with the ankle in plantarflexion, inversion, or eversion depending on which letter is being traced). The torso remains upright and stable, facing forward, with the core visibly engaged to maintain balance as the foot holds its extended position at the endpoint of the current letter's trajectory.

exercises.name: Ankle Circles
exercises.pose_description: Standing on one leg with light support from a chair or wall for balance. The opposite foot is lifted slightly off the ground and the ankle draws slow, controlled circles in the air, moving through full dorsiflexion, inversion, plantarflexion, and eversion. The knee of the circling leg remains relatively still.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright on one leg with a slight forward lean, hand lightly touching a chair or wall for balance, while the lifted foot completes a full circular motion with the ankle fully plantarflexed (toes pointed downward) and the leg turned inward in eversion, creating maximum ankle mobility. The supporting leg is nearly straight with a slight knee bend, the torso remains stable and squared forward, and the calf and anterior tibialis muscles appear engaged as the ankle reaches the bottom-most arc of its circular path.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Ankle Dorsiflexion
exercises.pose_description: Sit in a chair with one leg extended or knee bent at 90 degrees. Loop a resistance band around the ball of your foot and hold the ends of the band in both hands.
exercises.end_pose_description: Pull your toes upward toward your shin against the band resistance, creating tension along the front of your lower leg and the top of your foot. Slowly return to the starting position.

exercises.name: Seated Ankle Inversion and Eversion
exercises.pose_description: Sit with your back against a chair, one knee extended and the other bent slightly with foot flat. Keep your extended leg relaxed on a stool or ottoman.
exercises.end_pose_description: Rotate your extended foot inward (inversion) and outward (eversion) in controlled, deliberate motions. Move through a comfortable range without pain.

exercises.name: Arch Doming and Foot Intrinsic Strengthening
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright with your feet flat on the floor, toes pointed forward. Relax your foot completely and focus on the arch region of the sole of your foot.
exercises.end_pose_description: Without curling your toes, contract the intrinsic muscles of your foot to create an arch dome from heel to ball of foot. This should feel like a gentle lift and shortening of the arch; hold for 2 seconds and release.

exercises.name: Band-Assisted Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Kneel on one knee with the other leg extended forward, and loop a resistance band around the extended leg's foot. Maintain an upright torso with core engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently press your hips forward while using the band to assist the stretch on the hip flexor of the kneeling leg. Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning backward to maintain proper spinal alignment.

exercises.name: Band External Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright with your right elbow bent at 90 degrees, tucked against your side with your forearm pointing forward. Hold the resistance band in your right hand while anchoring the other end with your left hand or foot.
exercises.end_pose_description: Rotate your right forearm outward against the band resistance, moving your hand away from your body in an arc. Keep your elbow firmly against your ribs throughout the movement.

exercises.name: Band Shoulder Internal Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright with your left elbow bent at 90 degrees and tucked against your side, forearm pointing outward. Hold the resistance band in your left hand while anchoring the opposite end with your right hand or by stepping on it.
exercises.end_pose_description: Rotate your left forearm inward across your body against the band resistance, keeping your elbow stationary at your ribs. Complete all repetitions on one side before switching to the opposite shoulder.

exercises.name: Band Lat Pulldown
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright with your core engaged and the resistance band anchored above your head (looped over a door or frame). Hold both ends of the band with your arms extended overhead.
exercises.end_pose_description: Pull the band down toward your chest by bending your elbows and driving them past your ribs. Squeeze your shoulder blades and lats at the bottom before slowly returning to the starting position.

exercises.name: Band Pull-Aparts
exercises.target_area: Rotator Cuff, Scapular Stabilizers & Posterior Shoulder
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with arms extended in front at shoulder height, holding a resistance band with both hands slightly closer than shoulder-width apart. The hands pull the band apart by driving the arms outward and squeezing the shoulder blades together until the band touches the chest. The elbows stay straight and the shoulders remain depressed throughout.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with both arms extended directly out to the sides at shoulder height, elbows locked straight, and the resistance band stretched across the chest touching or nearly touching the torso. The shoulder blades are visibly retracted and squeezed together, creating prominent definition across the upper back and rear deltoids, with the chest slightly expanded and shoulders pulled down away from the ears.

exercises.name: Band-Resisted Shoulder Abduction
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart with a resistance band under both feet, holding the ends in each hand at your sides. Your arms are straight with the band taut and your posture is upright.
exercises.end_pose_description: Raise both arms out to your sides up to shoulder height against the band resistance, maintaining a slight elbow bend throughout. Your arms form a 90-degree angle with your torso at the peak of the movement.

exercises.name: Band Reverse Fly
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent. Hinge forward from your hips, keeping your back straight and your chest leaning towards the floor. Loop a resistance band under both feet and hold the handles with your arms hanging straight down, maintaining tension in the band.
exercises.end_pose_description: Raise both arms out to the sides and slightly backward in an arc, squeezing your shoulder blades together. Your arms should finish at shoulder height with elbows slightly bent throughout the movement.

exercises.name: Banded Copenhagen Adductor Exercise
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your side, propped up on your forearm, with your hips stacked and body straight. Place your top leg, fully extended, with your shin resting on an elevated surface. Your bottom leg is extended straight below your top leg, with a resistance band looped around both legs just above the knees.
exercises.end_pose_description: Lift your bottom leg up toward your top knee against the band resistance, focusing on inner thigh contraction. Lower with control and repeat.

exercises.name: Banded External Rotation at 90/90
exercises.pose_description: Stand with your right arm abducted to 90 degrees and elbow bent at 90 degrees, holding one end of a resistance band. Your forearm points downward and the band is anchored at shoulder height to your side.
exercises.end_pose_description: Rotate your forearm upward against the band resistance, keeping your elbow stationary at shoulder height. Your forearm finishes pointing upward, with the band providing controlled resistance throughout.

exercises.name: Banded Hip Internal Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright on a bench with both knees bent at 90 degrees and feet flat on the floor, with a resistance band looped around both feet. Maintain an upright posture with your core engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: Keeping your right knee stationary, rotate your right foot inward against the band resistance, then return to center. Switch sides and repeat with controlled movements.

exercises.name: Banded Pull-Apart for Shoulder Stability
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a resistance band with both hands at chest height with arms extended straight out in front of you. Your shoulders should be relaxed and core engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: Pull the band apart by moving your hands outward in an arc, squeezing your shoulder blades together and bringing your hands to shoulder width. Your arms should maintain a slight bend throughout the movement.

exercises.name: Banded Reverse Fly
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet hip-width apart and a resistance band held at chest height with both hands, arms bent and positioned in front of your body. Your shoulders should be relaxed and core engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: Pull the band apart and outward by opening your arms to the sides, squeezing your rear shoulder muscles and upper back. Your arms should end in a T position with elbows slightly bent.

exercises.name: Banded Shoulder Stabilizer Series
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright holding a resistance band with both hands. The exercise cycles through multiple positions: band pull-aparts at chest height, external rotation with elbows at sides, overhead press against band tension, and diagonal patterns. Throughout each movement, the shoulder blades are actively set down and back, the core is engaged, and the posture remains tall and aligned.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with shoulders pulled back and down, arms extended outward at shoulder height with the resistance band stretched wide across the chest, elbows slightly bent, and chest expanded with visible engagement through the upper back and rear deltoids. The core appears braced, spine neutral, and the entire posterior chain from shoulders through glutes shows tonal engagement against the band tension.

exercises.name: Banded Side-Lying Hip Adduction
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your side with a resistance band looped around both legs above the knees. Keep your bottom leg straight and your top leg bent with foot planted in front for stability.
exercises.end_pose_description: Lift your bottom leg upward against the band resistance, squeezing the inner thigh muscles. Hold briefly at the top before returning to the starting position.

exercises.name: Bicep Curls
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with a dumbbell or resistance band in each hand, arms at sides with palms facing forward. The forearms curl upward by bending the elbows, bringing the weights toward the shoulders while keeping the elbows pinned at the sides. The torso remains still without swaying, and the upper arms do not move.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with elbows bent at approximately 90 degrees, dumbbells held at shoulder height with palms facing forward. The upper arms remain stationary and close to the torso, while the forearms are vertical or slightly angled back toward the shoulders. The biceps appear fully contracted and engaged, creating visible muscle definition in the upper arms.

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.pose_description: Balancing on the left hand and right knee. The RIGHT arm reaches straight out in front, parallel to the ground, and the LEFT leg extends straight behind, also parallel to the ground. The body forms a straight line from fingertips to toes.
exercises.end_pose_description: On all fours in a tabletop position on the ground. The right arm is extended fully forward, parallel to the ground. The left leg is extended fully backward, parallel to the ground. The back is flat and level. Only the left hand and right knee remain on the ground.

exercises.name: Bird Dog Hold with Scapular Punch
exercises.target_area: Core Stability, Rotator Cuff & Scapular Control
exercises.pose_description: On hands and knees with right arm extended forward and left leg extended behind, parallel to the floor, in a standard bird dog position. From this hold, the extended arm performs a scapular punch by protracting the shoulder blade forward, pushing the hand further away from the body, then retracting back. The spine remains neutral and the core is fully braced.
exercises.end_pose_description: The athlete is in a quadruped position with the right arm fully extended forward and slightly protracted, with the shoulder blade pushed forward away from the torso, while the left leg remains extended straight behind parallel to the floor. The core, glutes, and shoulder stabilizers are visibly engaged with a rigid, neutral spine, and the person faces downward toward the ground with their gaze neutral.

exercises.name: Bird Dog with Core Stability Focus
exercises.target_area: Core stabilizers, hip extensors, lower back endurance
exercises.pose_description: On hands and knees in tabletop position with wrists directly under shoulders and knees under hips. The right arm extends forward and the left leg extends behind, both parallel to the floor, with an emphasis on maintaining a perfectly level pelvis and neutral spine. The movement is slow and deliberate with a prolonged hold at full extension, core braced throughout.
exercises.end_pose_description: The body forms a straight line from the extended right fingertips through the torso to the extended left heel, both limbs parallel to the floor at shoulder and hip height respectively, while the supporting left arm and right knee remain vertically aligned beneath the shoulders and hips. The core muscles are visibly tensioned, the pelvis is perfectly level with no rotation, and the spine maintains neutral alignment with the head in line with the extended arm. The person's torso is parallel to the ground with no sagging or hiking of the hips.

exercises.name: BOSU Ball Balance
exercises.pose_description: Standing on the dome side of a BOSU ball with feet hip-width apart or on a single leg. The knees are slightly bent, the core is engaged, and the arms are at sides or extended for balance. The body works to maintain equilibrium on the unstable surface while keeping the torso upright and the gaze directed forward at a fixed point.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands tall and stationary on the dome side of the BOSU ball with feet hip-width apart (or balanced on a single leg), knees slightly bent to maintain stability, torso upright and aligned over the base of support, core visibly engaged through a neutral spine, and arms either extended outward at shoulder height or positioned for counterbalance. The gaze is fixed forward at a focal point, with visible muscle engagement through the legs (quadriceps and glutes), core, and stabilizer muscles working to resist any wobbling on the unstable surface.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.pose_description: Standing about two feet in front of a bench or elevated surface with the top of one foot resting on the bench behind. The front foot is flat on the floor. The body lowers by bending the front knee to approximately 90 degrees while the back knee drops toward the floor. The torso stays upright, and the front knee tracks over the toes.
exercises.end_pose_description: The front leg is bent to approximately 90 degrees at the knee with the thigh nearly parallel to the ground, while the back knee hovers just above the floor in a deep lunge position. The torso remains upright and vertical, perpendicular to the ground, with the front quad and glute visibly tensed and engaged. The person faces forward with weight distributed through the front foot, creating a stable asymmetrical stance.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Calf Raises
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with a resistance band looped under the balls of both feet and holding the ends in your hands for tension. Your feet are hip-width apart and posture is tall.
exercises.end_pose_description: Rise up onto the balls of your feet, lifting your heels while pressing down through the band resistance. Pause at the top, feeling the engagement in your calves and the soles of your feet.

exercises.name: Calf Raises with Dumbbells
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with feet hip-width apart. Your weight is evenly distributed across the balls and heels of your feet.
exercises.end_pose_description: Rise up onto the balls of your feet, lifting your heels off the ground while maintaining an upright posture. Hold briefly at the top before lowering back down with control.

exercises.name: Calf Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Stand facing a wall with your hands on the wall at shoulder height. Step one leg back, keeping the heel on the ground.
exercises.end_pose_description: Lean forward into the wall, keeping the back leg straight and heel down. Feel the stretch in the calf of the back leg.

exercises.name: Calf Stretch with Band Against Wall
exercises.pose_description: Stand facing a wall with one leg forward in a lunge position and the back leg straight. Loop a resistance band around the ball of the back foot, holding the ends for assistance.
exercises.end_pose_description: Lean gently forward, using the band to help keep your back heel grounded as you feel a stretch in the calf muscle of the back leg. Maintain an upright torso and steady breathing.

exercises.name: Calf Stretch on Step
exercises.pose_description: Standing on the edge of a step with the balls of the feet on the step and the heels hanging off the back edge. One or both heels drop below the level of the step, creating a deep stretch in the calf muscles. Hands hold a railing or wall for balance, and the knees are straight to target the gastrocnemius.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright on a step with knees fully extended and straight, while both heels are dropped significantly below the step level, creating a pronounced downward angle at the ankles. The calf muscles appear visibly stretched and taut, with the body weight distributed through the balls of the feet on the step edge. Hands grip a railing or wall for stability, and the torso remains vertical and facing forward.

exercises.name: Calf Stretches Against Wall
exercises.pose_description: Stand facing a wall with your hands on the wall at shoulder height, feet hip-width apart. Place one leg forward with a slight knee bend and the other leg extended straight behind you.
exercises.end_pose_description: Keep your back heel on the ground and lean forward into the wall to feel a stretch in the calf of the extended back leg. Maintain an upright torso.

exercises.name: Calf Stretch with Band
exercises.pose_description: Sit with one leg extended and loop a resistance band around the ball of that foot, holding the ends in both hands. Keep your knee straight.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently pull the band toward your body to flex your foot upward (dorsiflexion), feeling a stretch in the calf and achilles tendon area. Hold for 30 seconds.

exercises.name: Calf Stretches
exercises.pose_description: Stand facing a wall with your hands placed on the wall at shoulder height for balance. Step the affected leg back about 12 inches.
exercises.end_pose_description: Keep the back heel on the ground and gently lean toward the wall, bending the front knee. Feel a gentle stretch in the calf of the back leg and hold for 30 seconds.

exercises.name: Cat-Camel Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Start on hands and knees with a neutral spine, hands under shoulders and knees under hips. Keep your head in neutral alignment with your spine.
exercises.end_pose_description: Arch your back gently by lowering your belly and lifting your head and tailbone toward the ceiling in the camel position. Then reverse by rounding your spine and tucking your chin.

exercises.name: Cat-Cow Stretch
exercises.pose_description: On hands and knees in tabletop position, wrists under shoulders, knees under hips. The spine is arched upward like a cat, rounding toward the ceiling, head tucked down. Wearing a gray t-shirt and dark shorts.
exercises.end_pose_description: The spine is fully extended and arched downward like a cow, with the chest pushed forward and upward toward the ceiling, shoulders dropped away from ears, and the head tilted back to gaze upward. The arms remain straight with elbows locked, wrists directly under shoulders, while the knees stay bent at 90 degrees under the hips, and the lower back and abdominal muscles appear fully engaged and stretched. The person's gaze is directed upward and slightly behind them.

exercises.name: Cervical Isometric Lateral Flexion
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright with shoulders relaxed and head in neutral position. Place your right hand on the right side of your head.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently press your head to the right into your hand while resisting movement with lateral neck muscles for 5-10 seconds. Repeat on left side.

exercises.name: Cervical Isometric Neck Extension
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright with good posture and head in neutral position. Place your hand on the back of your head with elbow bent.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently press the back of your head into your hand while resisting movement with your neck extensor muscles for 5-10 seconds.

exercises.name: Cervical Isometric Neck Flexion
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright with shoulders relaxed and head in neutral position. Place your hand on your forehead with elbow bent.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently press your forehead into your hand while resisting movement with your neck muscles for 5-10 seconds. Maintain neutral spine throughout.

exercises.name: Cervical Retraction with Isometric Hold
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright with shoulders relaxed and spine neutral. Gently tuck your chin and slide your head straight back, ensuring the back of your neck lengthens. Keep your gaze level and forward.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently draw your chin straight back (creating a double chin appearance) while keeping your gaze forward. Hold this retracted position while maintaining neutral spine.

exercises.name: Cervical Rotation Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright with good posture and shoulders relaxed. Head is facing forward in neutral position.
exercises.end_pose_description: Slowly rotate your head to the right, turning your chin toward your shoulder while maintaining upright posture. Hold 20-30 seconds and repeat on opposite side.

exercises.name: Chest Doorway Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Stand in a doorway with your affected arm raised to 90 degrees at the shoulder, elbow bent at 90 degrees, and forearm resting on the doorframe. Keep your chest upright and core engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently step forward into the doorway, feeling a stretch across your chest and anterior shoulder. Hold the stretch while maintaining good posture and controlled breathing.

exercises.name: Chest Stretch Corner
exercises.pose_description: Standing facing a corner of a room with one foot slightly forward. Both forearms are placed on the adjoining walls at approximately shoulder height with elbows bent at 90 degrees. The body leans into the corner until a stretch is felt across the chest and front of the shoulders. The core is engaged and the lower back does not arch excessively.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person faces directly into the corner with their torso upright and squared toward the walls, both forearms pressed flat against the adjoining walls at shoulder height with elbows bent at 90 degrees, creating a symmetrical frame. The chest is visibly expanded and drawn forward into the corner, with the pectoral muscles and front deltoids appearing stretched and engaged, while the core remains braced with a neutral spine.

exercises.name: Child's Pose
exercises.pose_description: A yoga child's pose: sitting back on the heels with the body folded completely forward and down, forehead on the ground, arms extended straight forward along the floor. The back is rounded and the person looks like they are bowing down.
exercises.end_pose_description: The body is fully folded forward in a deep forward bend, with the forehead resting on the ground and the torso collapsed over the thighs. The knees are bent at approximately 90 degrees with the buttocks sitting back toward the heels, while both arms extend straight forward along the floor with palms down, creating an elongated line from the hips through the fingertips. The entire spine appears rounded and stretched, with the shoulders relaxed and drawn downward, and the gaze directed downward toward the ground.

exercises.name: Child's Pose with Side Reach
exercises.target_area: Lower back, intercostal muscles, latissimus dorsi
exercises.pose_description: A person kneels with their hips resting back on their heels, knees slightly apart. The torso folds forward between the thighs, with the forehead gently resting on the floor. Arms are extended straight forward on the floor, palms flat.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains in a deep kneeling position with hips pressed back toward heels, torso folded forward and laterally flexed, with both arms extended diagonally across the floor toward one side and forehead resting on or near the ground. The entire body creates a curved line from the extended arms through the torso to the knees, with the ribcage and lateral core visibly elongated on the stretched side while the opposite side appears compressed.

exercises.name: Chin Tucks
exercises.pose_description: Stand tall with your back straight and shoulders relaxed. Look straight ahead, keeping your head in a neutral position with your ears aligned directly above your shoulders.
exercises.end_pose_description: Standing upright facing forward. The chin is drawn fully backward and downward, creating a pronounced double chin. The head is retracted straight back, not tilted up or down. The neck is elongated at the back.

exercises.name: Clam Shell Exercise with Band
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your side with hips and knees bent at 45 degrees and a resistance band above both knees. Keep your feet together and lower leg stable.
exercises.end_pose_description: Rotate your upper knee upward, opening it like a clamshell while keeping feet together. Pause at the top before closing back down.

exercises.name: Clamshells
exercises.pose_description: Side-lying hip exercise. The man is on his side like a sleeping position, facing the viewer. Head propped on bottom arm. Both knees are bent. The top leg's knee is raised up toward the ceiling while feet stay together. View from front showing the side-lying body clearly.
exercises.end_pose_description: Lying on the left side on the ground. Both knees are bent at about 45 degrees. Feet are stacked together and remain touching. The top (right) knee is lifted and opened up toward the ceiling at maximum abduction, like a clamshell opening.

exercises.name: Copenhagen Adduction
exercises.pose_description: Side-lying on the floor with the top leg resting on a bench or elevated surface. The bottom leg is hanging free beneath the bench. The person lifts the bottom leg up toward the bench by squeezing the inner thigh (adductors). The upper body is propped on the forearm in a side plank position. The top leg stays on the bench for support.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is in a side-lying position with the bottom leg lifted and pressed firmly against the top leg, creating a closed adductor squeeze where both legs are nearly parallel and stacked. The torso remains elevated on the forearm in a side plank, with the body forming a relatively straight line from head to knees, while the inner thighs visibly contract and engage. The person faces forward along the length of their body, with the bench supporting the top leg as the bottom leg reaches its maximum height at hip level.

exercises.name: Couch Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Kneeling on one knee with the back foot elevated against a wall or couch behind. Front leg is bent at 90 degrees with foot flat on the floor. Torso tall and upright, hands on the front knee for balance. Deep stretch visible in the hip flexor and quadriceps of the back leg.
exercises.end_pose_description: The torso is leaned back with the chest open and shoulders back, creating an extended arch through the spine while the back knee remains planted and the back foot pressed against the wall/couch behind. The front leg stays bent at 90 degrees with foot firmly planted, while the hip flexors and quadriceps of the back leg are maximally stretched and visibly engaged. The head is in neutral alignment or slightly back, and the hands may release from the front knee as the core stabilizes the extended position.

exercises.name: Cross-Body Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with one arm extended straight across the chest at shoulder height. The opposite hand cups the elbow or upper arm and gently pulls it closer to the body, creating a stretch across the posterior shoulder and upper back. The shoulders remain level and the torso does not twist.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with one arm crossed horizontally across the chest at shoulder height, elbow bent approximately 90 degrees, while the opposite hand firmly grasps and pulls the crossed arm closer to the body, creating a visible compression across the posterior shoulder and upper back. The shoulders remain level and square, the spine stays neutral without rotation, and the stretched shoulder blade appears retracted as the chest and anterior shoulder muscles visibly lengthen on the pulling side.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with arms extended straight toward the ceiling above the shoulders and both hips and knees bent to 90 degrees in a tabletop position. One arm reaches overhead toward the floor behind while the opposite leg extends straight out, lowering toward the floor without touching. The lower back remains pressed firmly into the ground throughout.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies supine on their back with one arm extended straight overhead toward the floor behind the head (shoulder flexed approximately 180 degrees) while the opposite leg extends fully straight, hovering just above the ground with the hip flexed at near 0 degrees; simultaneously, the other arm remains bent at 90 degrees with the hand reaching toward the ceiling and the opposite leg stays in the tabletop position with hip and knee both at 90 degrees. The lower back remains pressed flat against the ground, creating a diagonal line of tension across the torso from the extended arm to the extended leg, with visible abdominal and core musculature engaged to maintain spinal stability.

exercises.name: Dead Bug with Shoulder Reach
exercises.target_area: Core Stability, Lower Back & Shoulder Integration
exercises.pose_description: Lie flat on your back with hips and knees bent to 90 degrees, bringing your shins parallel to the floor. Extend both arms straight up towards the ceiling, hands positioned directly over your shoulders. Ensure your lower back remains pressed into the floor.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies supine with their lower back pressed flat against the floor, one arm extended overhead (nearly parallel to the ground) while the opposite leg extends straight out at hip height, creating a long diagonal line through the body. The reaching arm shows pronounced shoulder protraction with the scapula visibly lifted off the ribcage, while the core, obliques, and stabilizer muscles are clearly engaged to maintain the extended position and spinal stability.

exercises.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor. One hand rests on the upper chest and the other on the belly just below the ribcage. During inhalation, the belly rises prominently while the chest remains relatively still. During exhalation, the belly falls inward. The breathing is slow, deep, and controlled through the nose.
exercises.end_pose_description: Person lies supine with knees bent at approximately 90 degrees and feet flat on the floor, shoulders relaxed against the ground. The abdomen is maximally expanded and visibly distended outward, while the chest remains relatively stationary, with the hand on the belly lifted slightly upward by the rounded, expanded midsection. The face is relaxed looking upward, neck neutral, with deep abdominal and core muscles visibly engaged to support the full inhalation.

exercises.name: Doorway Chest Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Stand in a doorway with your affected arm raised to 90 degrees, elbow bent, and your forearm against the door frame. Step one foot forward into a slight lunge position.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently lean your body forward through the doorway, feeling a stretch across your chest and front shoulder. Maintain the stretch for 20-30 seconds while keeping your core engaged.

exercises.name: Doorway Pec Stretch with Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Stand in a doorway with one arm raised to 90 degrees, elbow bent, and forearm resting against the doorframe. Step one foot forward slightly.
exercises.end_pose_description: Rotate your torso away from the raised arm, deepening the stretch across your chest and shoulder. Feel the stretch intensify through your pectoral muscles.

exercises.name: Doorway Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Standing in a doorway facing through it. Both arms are raised to shoulder height with elbows bent at 90 degrees, forearms pressed against each side of the door frame. The body leans forward through the doorway to stretch the chest. One foot is slightly ahead of the other.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands in the doorway with both arms raised to shoulder height, elbows bent at 90 degrees with forearms pressed firmly against the door frame on either side, while the torso leans forward through the opening with the chest stretched and shoulders pulled back slightly. The legs remain in a staggered stance with one foot forward, the back straight or slightly arched as the body extends into the stretch. The face looks forward through the doorway, with visible tension across the chest, shoulders, and anterior deltoids.

exercises.name: Double Knee-to-Chest
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with both knees pulled up toward the chest simultaneously. Both hands wrap around the shins or behind the thighs, hugging the knees close. The lower back rounds gently into the floor, the tailbone lifts slightly, and the head and shoulders remain relaxed on the ground.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies supine on their back with both knees drawn maximally toward the chest, creating acute angles at the hips and knees (approximately 90 degrees each), while both hands clasp firmly around the shins or behind the thighs. The lower back is fully rounded and pressed into the floor with the tailbone lifted, the head remains neutral on the ground, and the abdominal and hip flexor muscles appear engaged and contracted as the body forms a compact, folded position.

exercises.name: Double Leg Calf Raise
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with feet hip-width apart, lightly holding a wall or railing for balance. Both heels rise simultaneously as high as possible, pushing up onto the balls of the feet. The knees remain straight, the body is tall, and the calf muscles fully contract at the top of the movement.
exercises.end_pose_description: The body is fully upright and vertical, balanced on the balls of both feet with heels lifted as high as possible off the ground, creating a visible arch through the foot. The legs are completely straight with no knee bend, the torso is tall and neutral, and the calf muscles are visibly contracted and bulging along the back of the lower leg from the ankle to below the knee. The person faces forward with one or both hands lightly touching a wall or railing for minimal balance support.

exercises.name: Double-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back on a mat with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. Your arms are at your sides with palms facing down.
exercises.end_pose_description: Push through your heels to lift your hips toward the ceiling, creating a straight line from knees to shoulders. Squeeze your glutes at the top before lowering back down.

exercises.name: Downward Facing Dog
exercises.pose_description: Starting from hands and knees, the figure pushes hips up and back into an inverted V shape. Arms are straight and extended overhead pressing into the floor, head between the upper arms looking toward the feet. Legs are straight with heels pressing toward the ground. Back is flat forming a straight line from hands to hips.
exercises.end_pose_description: The body forms a perfect inverted V-shape with the head positioned between fully extended arms, eyes gazing down toward the feet planted on the ground. The hips are pushed high and back, creating a straight diagonal line from the hands through the torso to the heels, with legs fully extended and shoulder blades drawn down the back, visibly engaging the core and shoulder stabilizers.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Deadlifts with Posterior Chain Focus
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with arms straight. Engage your core and maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement.
exercises.end_pose_description: Hinge at the hips while keeping your shins relatively vertical, lowering the dumbbells down the front of your legs. Feel a stretch in your hamstrings and calves as you descend, then drive through your heels to return to standing.

exercises.name: Dumbbell External Rotation at 90/90
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back on a bench with your shoulder abducted to 90 degrees and your elbow bent at 90 degrees, holding a light dumbbell. Your upper arm is perpendicular to your body.
exercises.end_pose_description: Rotate the dumbbell upward, bringing your forearm toward vertical while keeping your upper arm stationary at 90 degrees of abduction. Slowly return to the neutral position.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Farmer Carry
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright holding a dumbbell in one or both hands at your sides with your shoulders packed back and down. Engage your core and maintain an upright posture.
exercises.end_pose_description: Walk forward while maintaining shoulder stability and neutral spine, keeping the dumbbell(s) stable at your side. Maintain scapular control throughout the movement.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Farmer's Carry
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with dumbbells held at your sides with a neutral grip and your shoulders packed down and back. Your core is engaged and your posture is tall.
exercises.end_pose_description: Walk forward while maintaining perfect upright posture with shoulders retracted and scapulae stabilized. Your arms remain straight at your sides throughout the movement.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Goblet Squats
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell vertically at chest height with both hands. Keep your chest up and core engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: Lower into a squat by bending your hips and knees, keeping the dumbbell at chest level and weight in your heels. Drive through your heels to return to standing, maintaining an upright posture throughout.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Hip Thrusts
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor hip-width apart, and a dumbbell resting across your hips. Your arms are at your sides for support.
exercises.end_pose_description: Drive through your heels and lift your hips high, creating a straight line from knees to shoulders while holding the dumbbell secure. Squeeze your glutes firmly at the top before lowering.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Pullovers
exercises.pose_description: Lie perpendicular across a bench with your upper back supported and feet on the floor, holding a single dumbbell with both hands above your chest. Your shoulders are in a relaxed position.
exercises.end_pose_description: Lower the dumbbell in an arc motion behind and above your head, allowing a stretch across your chest and anterior shoulder. Your hips remain on or near the bench throughout the movement.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlifts
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with a slight bend in your knees. Your weight is distributed through the entire foot.
exercises.end_pose_description: Hinge at the hips while maintaining a neutral spine, lowering the dumbbells toward the ground and feeling a stretch in your hamstrings. Return to standing by driving through your feet.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Rows
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with a slight forward hinge at the hips. Keep your core engaged and your back neutral.
exercises.end_pose_description: Pull both dumbbells up toward your ribcage, squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top. Your elbows should stay close to your body throughout the movement.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Single-Leg Deadlift
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright on one leg with a slight bend in the standing knee. Hold a dumbbell in the hand opposite your standing leg, keeping your arm extended downwards. Maintain a straight back and lifted chest.
exercises.end_pose_description: Hinge at the hip while extending your free leg behind you for counterbalance, lowering the dumbbell toward the ground. Return to standing by driving through your heel and squeezing your glute.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Step-Ups
exercises.pose_description: Stand facing a low step or bench, holding dumbbells at your sides with a neutral grip. Keep your chest upright and core engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: Step up onto the bench with the unaffected leg first, then bring the affected leg up to meet it. Step back down with control, leading with the affected leg.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Step-Ups with Emphasis on Stance Leg Stability
exercises.pose_description: Stand facing a sturdy step or bench with dumbbells held at your sides. Place one foot on the step with your weight distributed evenly across the entire foot.
exercises.end_pose_description: Drive through your front heel to step up onto the bench, bringing your rear foot to meet it. Slowly step back down with control, emphasizing stability through the foot and ankle of your stance leg.

exercises.name: Dynamic Adductor Stretch with Hip Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet wide apart in a staggered stance with hands on your hips. Keep your back straight and core engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: Lunge toward one side while rotating your hips, feeling a dynamic stretch along the inner thigh. Return to center and alternate sides.

exercises.name: Eccentric Biceps Curl with Band
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a resistance band anchored under your feet with both hands at shoulder height. Your elbows are bent at 90 degrees and tucked close to your torso.
exercises.end_pose_description: Slowly lower your hands toward your thighs in a controlled manner over 3-4 seconds, keeping your elbows stationary and close to your body. Your arms are nearly straight at the end of the eccentric phase.

exercises.name: Eccentric Calf Lowering
exercises.pose_description: Standing on the edge of a step with the balls of both feet on the step. Starting from a full calf raise on both feet, the weight transfers to one leg, and that heel slowly lowers below the step level over three to five seconds. The knee remains straight, and the opposite foot assists for the return to the top position.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands on a step with one leg straight and that heel dropped significantly below step level, creating a deep calf stretch with the foot dorsiflexed (toes pointing upward), while the opposite leg is bent with foot lifted off the step to assist with balance. The torso remains upright and perpendicular to the ground, with engaged calf muscles visibly stretched on the lowered leg and the standing leg's calf fully lengthened.

exercises.name: Eccentric Hamstring Curls
exercises.pose_description: Lie face down on a bench or stability ball with legs extended and toes pointed toward the floor. Place hands by your sides for light support.
exercises.end_pose_description: Bend both knees to bring heels toward glutes, then use both legs to extend back. Slowly lower yourself using only the affected leg over 3-4 seconds.

exercises.name: Elbow Flexion with Dumbbell
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with your arms at your sides, holding a light dumbbell in your affected arm with palm facing forward. Your elbow is fully extended but not locked.
exercises.end_pose_description: Bend your elbow to bring the dumbbell up toward your shoulder in a slow, controlled bicep curl motion. Lower the weight back down with control.

exercises.name: Elbow Range of Motion Pendulum
exercises.pose_description: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and bend forward slightly at the waist, letting your affected arm hang down naturally from your shoulder. Keep your arm relaxed and loose.
exercises.end_pose_description: Using a small pendulum motion from your shoulder, gently swing your arm forward and backward in a small arc. Allow gravity to assist the motion while keeping your elbow and wrist relaxed.

exercises.name: External Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with the working arm bent at 90 degrees at the elbow, elbow pinned to the side of the body. A resistance band or light dumbbell is held in the hand. The forearm rotates outward away from the body while keeping the elbow firmly against the torso, moving through approximately 45 degrees of external rotation.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with the working arm still bent 90 degrees at the elbow, pinned against the ribcage, but the forearm is rotated outward away from the centerline of the body at approximately 45 degrees. The forearm appears nearly perpendicular to the body's sagittal plane, with visible tension in the shoulder and upper back muscles, particularly the posterior deltoid and rotator cuff, while the opposite arm hangs relaxed at the side.

exercises.name: Farmer's Carry
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with your shoulders packed back and core engaged. Maintain a neutral spine throughout.
exercises.end_pose_description: Walk forward for a set distance or time while maintaining excellent posture and keeping the dumbbells at your sides. Focus on stable, controlled steps with no spinal deviation.

exercises.name: Figure-4 Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with both knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Cross one ankle over the opposite knee to create a figure-4 shape.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently pull your thigh toward your chest while keeping your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor. Maintain the stretch for the prescribed duration without bouncing.

exercises.name: Finger Abduction and Adduction
exercises.pose_description: Sit with your hand flat on a table, fingers spread slightly apart. Keep your palm and forearm relaxed against the table.
exercises.end_pose_description: Slowly spread all fingers apart, moving them away from the middle finger. Return to starting position and repeat without forcing movement.

exercises.name: Finger Flexion Exercises
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright with your forearm resting on a table, palm facing up. Keep your fingers extended and relaxed.
exercises.end_pose_description: Slowly curl all fingers into a gentle fist, bending at each joint. Hold briefly without forcing any pain in the affected finger.

exercises.name: Finger Tendon Glides
exercises.pose_description: Standing or seated with one hand extended in front, palm facing away. The fingers move through a series of positions: straight extension, hook fist (tips bent to pads), full fist, straight fist (fingers curled at knuckles only), and tabletop (fingers bent at knuckles to 90 degrees with fingertips pointing forward). Each position is held briefly before transitioning.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with one arm extended at shoulder height, palm facing away, fingers curled into a tabletop position where the metacarpophalangeal joints are bent at approximately 90 degrees while the fingertips point directly forward and the hand appears flat across the top. The forearm remains straight and parallel to the ground, with visible tension in the finger extensors and intrinsic hand muscles creating definition across the back of the hand and fingers.

exercises.name: Fire Hydrants
exercises.pose_description: On hands and knees in tabletop position with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips. One knee remains bent at 90 degrees and lifts out to the side, opening the hip like a fire hydrant, to approximately hip height. The spine stays neutral, the core is braced, and the pelvis does not rotate or shift.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains in quadruped position with hands and knees planted firmly on the ground, while one leg is abducted outward with the knee bent at 90 degrees, lifted to approximately hip height and pointing perpendicular to the body. The lifted side's glute medius and hip abductor muscles are visibly engaged and contracted, the spine maintains a neutral line from head to hips, and the torso faces downward without any rotation or pelvic shift.

exercises.name: Foam Roller Calf
exercises.pose_description: Seated on the floor with legs extended and a foam roller positioned under both calves. Hands are placed behind the hips on the floor, lifting the buttocks slightly off the ground. The body rolls forward and backward, moving the roller from just above the ankles to below the knees, applying pressure along the calf muscles.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is seated on the floor with their torso leaning slightly backward, arms extended behind them with hands pressing into the floor to support lifted hips, while both legs are extended and the foam roller is positioned at the furthest point of the roll (either fully toward the ankles or fully toward the knees, depending on direction). The calf muscles appear maximally engaged and compressed against the foam roller, with the body weight distributed between the hands and the roller contact point.

exercises.name: Foam Roller IT Band
exercises.pose_description: Lying on one side with a foam roller positioned under the outer thigh between the hip and the knee. The bottom leg is extended straight, and the top leg may cross over in front with the foot flat on the floor for support and pressure control. The hands and forearms support the upper body off the ground as the body rolls slowly up and down the roller along the IT band.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is positioned on their side with the foam roller pressed firmly into the upper outer thigh/hip area, body weight supported through forearms and hands on the ground. The bottom leg is fully extended straight along the ground, while the top leg is crossed over with knee bent and foot planted in front of the body for stability, creating a stacked side-lying position. The IT band, glute medius, and hip stabilizer muscles appear engaged and compressed against the roller.

exercises.name: Foam Roller Quad
exercises.pose_description: Lying face down in a modified plank position with a foam roller positioned under the front of both thighs. The forearms support the upper body, and the toes may be off the ground. The body rolls slowly forward and backward, moving the roller from just above the kneecaps to the hip flexors, applying pressure to the quadriceps.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is in a prone plank position with forearms flat on the ground, elbows bent at approximately 90 degrees, and the foam roller positioned at the highest point on the thighs near the hip flexors. The body is nearly horizontal and parallel to the ground with core muscles visibly engaged, legs extended straight behind with toes lightly touching or hovering, and the quadriceps appear compressed and engaged against the roller as the upper body weight presses down through the forearms.

exercises.name: Foam Roller Thoracic Extension
exercises.pose_description: Lying on back with a foam roller positioned horizontally under the mid-back at the level of the shoulder blades. Knees are bent with feet flat on the floor, and hands are clasped behind the head to support the neck. The upper back gently arches over the roller, extending the thoracic spine while the hips remain on the floor.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies on their back with the foam roller positioned under the mid-back, their chest prominently arched backward in maximum thoracic extension while hips remain planted on the floor and knees stay bent with feet flat. The hands remain clasped behind the head with elbows spread wide, and the head gently extends back without straining the neck, creating a pronounced C-curve through the upper spine that stretches the chest and anterior shoulders. The abdominal and hip flexor muscles appear lengthened while the upper back musculature is visibly engaged around the roller.

exercises.name: Forearm Plank on Knees
exercises.pose_description: Start on your knees with forearms on the ground, elbows under shoulders, and hands flat or in fists. Keep your core engaged and body in a straight line from knees to head.
exercises.end_pose_description: Hold a static plank position, maintaining neutral wrist position and steady breathing. This builds core stability while gently conditioning the wrist in a supported position.

exercises.name: Forearm Pronation Wall Walk
exercises.pose_description: Stand facing a wall, about 12 inches away with your feet hip-width apart. Place your affected palm flat against the wall at waist height with your arm extended.
exercises.end_pose_description: Rotate your forearm so your palm slowly rolls away from the wall, rotating outward as far as comfortable. Hold the end position, then rotate your palm back to face the wall.

exercises.name: Forearm Pronation/Supination with Band
exercises.pose_description: Sit with your elbow bent at 90 degrees, upper arm against your body, palm facing down with a resistance band in your hand. Your forearm is parallel to the ground.
exercises.end_pose_description: Rotate your forearm so your palm faces upward against light band resistance, then rotate back to palms down. Move slowly through the full range of motion.

exercises.name: Forearm Supination Isometric Hold
exercises.pose_description: Sit with your elbow bent at 90 degrees against your torso, palm facing upward, holding a light dumbbell. Your opposite hand is positioned to provide gentle resistance.
exercises.end_pose_description: Hold the supinated position (palm up) while your opposite hand applies gentle resistance, creating an isometric contraction. Maintain steady pressure without movement for the prescribed duration.

exercises.name: Gastrocnemius and Soleus Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Stand facing a wall with one leg extended behind you, heel planted firmly on the ground and toes pointing forward. Place your hands on the wall at shoulder height for support.
exercises.end_pose_description: Keep your back leg straight and lean forward into the wall, feeling a stretch in the calf of the extended leg. Hold this position and feel the tension in the gastrocnemius and soleus muscles.

exercises.name: Gentle Finger Stretching
exercises.pose_description: Sit comfortably with one hand resting on your lap. Use your other hand to gently hold the affected finger at the base.
exercises.end_pose_description: Carefully extend the affected finger backward using gentle pressure from your other hand. Feel a mild stretch along the finger without pain.

exercises.name: Gentle Stretching
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with feet shoulder-width apart. Both arms are raised straight overhead with fingers interlaced, palms facing the ceiling, stretching tall. Wearing a gray t-shirt and dark shorts. White background.
exercises.end_pose_description: The torso is gently leaned to one side with the interlaced hands stretched overhead and slightly back, creating a visible elongation along the entire side body from the hip to the fingertips. The feet remain planted shoulder-width apart on the ground, legs straight but not locked, and the head follows the natural curve of the spine in a neutral position. The lateral core, obliques, and shoulder muscles show subtle engagement as the stretch deepens.

exercises.name: Gentle Wrist Extension Strengthening
exercises.pose_description: Sit with your forearm resting on a table or armrest, palm facing down with your hand hanging slightly off the edge. Keep your elbow supported and bent at 90 degrees.
exercises.end_pose_description: Slowly lift your hand and fingers upward, extending through the wrist joint. Pause at the top, then lower back down in a controlled manner.

exercises.name: Gentle Wrist Flexion Strengthening
exercises.pose_description: Sit with your forearm resting on a table or armrest, palm facing up with your hand hanging slightly off the edge. Keep your elbow bent at 90 degrees and supported.
exercises.end_pose_description: Slowly curl your fingers and hand upward toward your body, lifting only through the wrist joint. Pause briefly at the top, then lower back down to the starting position.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with knees bent at approximately 90 degrees, feet flat on the floor hip-width apart, arms resting at sides with palms down. The hips press upward by squeezing the glutes until the body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees. The weight is driven through the heels, and the core remains engaged at the top.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies supine with shoulders and head remaining on the ground, hips thrust upward to create a straight diagonal line from knees through torso to shoulders. Knees are bent at approximately 90 degrees with feet flat on the floor, arms pressed into the ground at the sides with palms down for stability. The glutes, hamstrings, and lower back are visibly contracted and engaged, with the pelvis tilted upward and core muscles tight.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge Hold
exercises.target_area: Glutes, lower back extensors, core stabilizers
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with knees bent at approximately 90 degrees, feet flat on the floor hip-width apart, arms at sides. The hips are pressed upward into the bridge position, forming a straight line from shoulders to knees, and this position is sustained for the prescribed duration. The glutes remain fully contracted, the core is braced, and the hips do not drop throughout the hold.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies supine with their upper back and shoulders firmly planted on the ground, hips thrust upward in a straight, level line parallel to the ground, creating a bridge shape from shoulders to knees. The knees are bent at 90 degrees with feet flat and hip-width apart, while arms rest at the sides with palms down. The glutes and lower back are visibly contracted and engaged, forming a taut, elevated line across the torso and thighs.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge with Isometric Hold
exercises.target_area: Gluteal muscles, hip extensors, lower back
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with knees bent at approximately 90 degrees, feet flat on the floor hip-width apart, arms at sides. The hips are lifted to the top position forming a straight line from shoulders to knees, and this position is held isometrically for a sustained duration. The glutes are maximally squeezed, the core is braced, and the hips do not drop.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies supine with hips thrust upward in a straight diagonal line from shoulders to knees, creating a bridge position where the torso is elevated and parallel to the ground. The knees remain bent at approximately 90 degrees with feet flat and hip-width apart, while the glutes appear maximally contracted and tightened, the core is visibly braced, and the shoulders remain flat against the floor. The arms rest at the sides with palms down, and the face points upward toward the ceiling with the body creating a strong horizontal platform from knees to shoulders.

exercises.name: Glute Bridges
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with knees bent at approximately 90 degrees, feet flat on the floor hip-width apart, arms resting at sides. Hips are lifted high off the ground forming a straight line from shoulders to knees, with glutes fully squeezed at the top.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies supine with knees bent at 90 degrees and feet flat on the floor, hips thrust upward to create a straight diagonal line from knees through torso to shoulders. The glutes are maximally contracted and appear prominently rounded, the core is visibly engaged and tight, and the arms rest flat on the ground alongside the body for stability. The person's gaze points upward toward the ceiling.

exercises.name: Glute Kickbacks with Dumbbell
exercises.pose_description: Start in a tabletop position with a dumbbell resting in the crease of your right knee. Keep your core engaged and spine neutral throughout.
exercises.end_pose_description: Drive your right leg backward and upward, extending your hip while keeping your knee bent at 90 degrees. Squeeze your glute at the top before returning to start position.

exercises.name: Glute Squeezes
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with both knees bent and feet flat on the floor, positioned about hip-width apart. Keep your arms relaxed at your sides.
exercises.end_pose_description: Squeeze the buttock muscles tightly, holding the contraction as if preventing something from passing. Hold for 5 seconds while maintaining normal breathing before releasing.

exercises.name: Grip Strengthening
exercises.pose_description: Standing or seated with the arm at the side or supported on a surface. The hand squeezes a grip strengthener, stress ball, or tennis ball, closing all fingers firmly around the object with maximum contraction. The wrist remains in a neutral position, and the forearm muscles visibly contract during the squeeze.
exercises.end_pose_description: The hand is fully closed into a tight fist around the grip strengthener, with all fingers curled inward at maximum contraction and the thumb pressing against the fingers. The forearm is prominently flexed with visible muscle definition in the flexor digitorum and flexor carpi radialis, while the wrist remains neutral and straight, and the arm stays relaxed at the side or on the support surface with the elbow at approximately 90 degrees.

exercises.name: Gentle Grip Strengthening with Dumbbell
exercises.pose_description: Sit comfortably with your arm resting on your lap, holding a light dumbbell with a neutral grip. Your hand is relaxed at the starting position.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently squeeze your fingers around the dumbbell, creating moderate tension without pain. Hold the squeeze for 2-3 seconds before releasing to the starting position.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Pallof Press
exercises.target_area: Core, Lower Back Stabilization & Rotational Control
exercises.pose_description: In a half-kneeling position with the inside knee down and the outside foot forward, positioned perpendicular to a cable or band anchor point. Both hands hold the band or cable handle at the chest. The arms press straight forward, extending fully away from the chest, resisting the rotational pull of the band. The torso remains perfectly upright and square, the core braces against rotation.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is in a half-kneeling position with arms fully extended straight forward at shoulder height, elbows locked, gripping the cable handle with both hands pressed away from the chest. The torso remains perfectly vertical and squared forward with no rotation, core visibly braced, while the back and oblique muscles appear engaged in resisting the lateral pull of the cable. The head remains neutral facing forward, shoulders packed and stable.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Shoulder Rotations with Band
exercises.target_area: Rotator Cuff, External Rotators & Shoulder Stability
exercises.pose_description: In a half-kneeling position with one knee on the floor and the opposite foot flat in front, hip and knee at 90 degrees. A resistance band is anchored to the side, and the working arm is bent at 90 degrees at the elbow with the elbow at the side. The forearm rotates outward against the band and returns inward, training external rotation. The torso remains tall and the core is engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains in half-kneeling position with torso upright and squared forward, while the working arm is rotated outward so the forearm points away from the body at approximately 90 degrees of external rotation at the shoulder, with the elbow still bent at 90 degrees and tucked at the side. The resistance band is fully stretched, creating visible tension across the front of the shoulder and chest, with the rotator cuff and shoulder stabilizers visibly engaged.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Single-Arm Dumbbell Press
exercises.pose_description: Kneel on one knee with the opposite foot forward in a staggered stance, keeping your torso upright. Hold a dumbbell at shoulder height on one side with your elbow at 90 degrees.
exercises.end_pose_description: Press the dumbbell straight up overhead while maintaining a neutral spine and preventing any rotation of your torso. Lower the dumbbell back to shoulder height under control.

exercises.name: Half Kneeling Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.pose_description: Position yourself in a half-kneeling stance with one knee down and one foot forward, holding a dumbbell in the hand opposite your forward leg. Your torso is upright and core is engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: Row the dumbbell up toward your hip by driving your elbow back and retracting your scapula, keeping your torso stable and square. Your shoulder blade pulls toward your spine at the top of the movement.

exercises.name: Hamstring Curls
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright holding onto a chair or counter for balance. One foot is lifted behind the body by bending the knee, bringing the heel toward the buttock while keeping the thighs parallel. The standing leg remains straight with a slight knee bend, and the torso stays upright.
exercises.end_pose_description: The standing leg remains nearly straight with minimal knee bend, while the working leg's knee is bent at approximately 90 degrees with the heel pulled as close as possible to the glutes, creating a sharp angle at the knee joint. The torso remains upright and vertical, facing forward with the person still gripping the chair/counter for stability, and the hamstring and glute muscles of the lifted leg are visibly contracted and engaged.

exercises.name: Hamstring Sets
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with both legs extended on the floor. Keep your affected leg relaxed.
exercises.end_pose_description: Bend the affected knee slightly and press the back of the knee down into the floor, tightening the hamstring muscle. Hold the contraction for 5 seconds without moving.

exercises.name: Hamstring Stretch with Band
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with one leg bent and one leg extended. Loop a resistance band around the foot of the extended leg.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently pull the band toward your torso to straighten the leg and deepen the hamstring stretch. Keep your lower back flat on the floor throughout.

exercises.name: Hamstring Stretch with Strap
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with one leg extended on the floor. A strap, towel, or belt is looped around the foot of the other leg, which is raised straight up toward the ceiling with the knee as straight as possible. Both hands hold the ends of the strap and gently pull the leg closer, deepening the hamstring stretch. The hips remain flat on the floor.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies supine on their back with their lower back and hips pressed firmly into the floor. One leg remains extended straight on the ground while the other leg is pulled nearly vertical toward the chest, with the knee nearly straight and the foot dorsiflexed, as both hands grip the strap around the foot and draw it slightly past vertical toward the torso. The hamstring, calf, and posterior chain of the elevated leg appear fully engaged and stretched, while the torso remains flat and stable against the ground.

exercises.name: Hamstring Stretches
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with both legs extended on the floor. Keep your unaffected leg flat and relaxed.
exercises.end_pose_description: Slowly pull the affected leg toward your chest by grasping behind the thigh with both hands, keeping the knee slightly bent. Hold the gentle stretch for 30 seconds.

exercises.name: Heel Drops
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright, holding a railing for balance. Position the balls of both feet on the edge of an elevated step, allowing the heels to extend freely off the back. Slightly raise both heels so you are standing on the balls of your feet, ready to begin the exercise.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands on a step in profile, with one leg supporting their weight while the opposite heel is lowered well below the step level, creating a deep dorsiflexion stretch through the calf. The supporting leg is nearly straight with minimal knee bend, the torso remains upright and stable, and the hand grips the railing for balance as the lowered calf muscle appears fully lengthened and engaged. The person faces forward with shoulders square to the direction of travel.

exercises.name: Heel Slides
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back, viewed from the side. One leg is straight on the ground. The other knee is bent with the foot flat on the floor near the buttocks, heel touching the ground. Arms at sides.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains supine on their back, with the bent knee fully extended straight along the floor, heel still in contact with the ground, creating a long line from hip to foot. The quadriceps and hip flexors appear visibly engaged and contracted as the leg reaches full extension. The opposite leg remains straight on the floor, arms stay at sides, and the torso remains flat against the ground.

exercises.name: Heel-Toe Walking
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with feet together and arms relaxed at your sides. Maintain a tall posture with your gaze directed forward.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright with one leg extended forward in a straight line, heel planted on the ground directly in front of the other foot's toes, while the back leg remains straight with the toe pushing off or just lifting. The torso is tall and vertical, core engaged, with arms extended laterally at shoulder height for balance, and the head faces forward with eyes focused ahead. The forward leg's hip flexors and anterior tibialis are visibly engaged, while the calf and posterior chain of the back leg show tension from the stabilization effort.

exercises.name: Heel Walks
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with arms at your sides or hands on a railing for light balance support. Lift your toes off the ground so your weight is on your heels.
exercises.end_pose_description: Walk forward slowly with your toes pointing upward and heels on the ground, maintaining activation in your shin muscles. Continue walking at a controlled pace for the prescribed distance.

exercises.name: Hip Abduction with Resistance Band
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with a resistance band looped around both legs just above the knees. Keep a slight bend in both knees for stability.
exercises.end_pose_description: Step the affected leg out to the side against the band resistance, maintaining an upright posture. Return to starting position with controlled movement.

exercises.name: Hip Abduction with Band
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your side with legs extended and a resistance band looped around both thighs. Keep your torso stable and your lower leg as a base.
exercises.end_pose_description: Lift your top leg upward against the band resistance, maintaining a straight alignment. Lower down without touching your legs together and repeat.

exercises.name: Hip Circles
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with hands on hips and feet shoulder-width apart. The hips draw large, smooth circles in a clockwise or counterclockwise direction, rotating through flexion, lateral tilt, extension, and the opposite lateral tilt. The upper body remains as still as possible and the knees stay slightly soft.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright with hands resting on hips, feet shoulder-width apart, and knees slightly bent. At the peak of the hip circle, the hips are maximally rotated to one side (either fully extended backward or tilted laterally), creating a visible asymmetrical line from shoulders through hips, while the upper body and head remain centered and still, facing forward. The oblique muscles on the extended side appear engaged and slightly lengthened, contrasting with the compressed appearance on the opposite side.

exercises.name: Seated Hip External Rotation with Band
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with one ankle crossed over the opposite knee, forming a figure-4 position. Place a resistance band around the knee of the raised leg.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently press the raised knee outward against the band resistance, rotating at the hip to open up the hip flexor and external rotators. Maintain an upright posture throughout the movement.

exercises.name: Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.pose_description: In a half-kneeling lunge position with the right knee on the floor directly under the right hip, and the left foot flat on the floor in front with the left knee bent at 90 degrees. The torso is tall and upright, hips are pressed gently forward, and a deep stretch is felt in the front of the right hip and thigh. Hands rest on the front knee or at the waist.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is in a deep half-kneeling lunge with the right knee planted on the ground directly beneath the hip, while the left leg is positioned forward with the knee bent at approximately 90 degrees and foot flat. The torso remains tall and vertical, with the hips pressed forward in a tucked position, creating visible tension and engagement through the front of the right hip flexor and quadriceps. The person faces forward with hands either resting on the front knee or positioned at the waist, and the body appears symmetric from a lateral view.

exercises.name: Hip Hinge
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with feet hip-width apart and knees slightly bent. The torso hinges forward from the hips, pushing the buttocks backward while keeping the back flat and chest proud. The arms hang naturally or a dowel rod is held along the spine to maintain spinal alignment. The movement stops when the torso reaches approximately parallel to the floor.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is bent forward at the hips with their torso nearly parallel to the ground, knees slightly bent, and buttocks pushed backward, while the spine remains neutral and straight from head to tailbone. The arms hang straight down or along a dowel rod on the back, and the hamstrings and glutes appear visibly engaged and tensioned. The head remains neutral in line with the spine, and the person's gaze is directed slightly downward.

exercises.name: Internal Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with the working arm bent at 90 degrees at the elbow, elbow pinned to the side of the body. A resistance band or cable is held in the hand. The forearm rotates inward across the body toward the stomach, working the internal rotators of the shoulder. The elbow stays firmly at the side throughout the movement.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with the working arm bent at 90 degrees at the elbow, forearm rotated inward across the front of the body toward the midline/stomach, with the elbow remaining pinned against the ribcage. The shoulder internal rotators and anterior chest muscles appear visibly engaged and contracted, creating tension across the front shoulder and chest.

exercises.name: Intrinsic Foot Muscle Strengthening
