exercises.pose_description: Sit upright with bare feet flat on the floor, toes relaxed and spread naturally. Keep your heel in place throughout the exercise.
exercises.end_pose_description: Curl your toes downward to create an arch in your foot, shortening the distance from your heel to the base of your toes. Maintain the heel position without curling it.

exercises.name: Inversion/Eversion with Band
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with your injured leg extended, a resistance band looped around the ball of your foot. Your knee remains straight and stable throughout.
exercises.end_pose_description: Turn your foot inward (inversion) and outward (eversion) against the band resistance, moving through a comfortable range. Control the movement in both directions.

exercises.name: Isometric Cervical Extension
exercises.pose_description: Standing or seated upright with one or both hands clasped behind the head. The head pushes backward into the hands with sustained effort while the hands resist the movement, creating an isometric contraction of the neck extensors. No visible movement occurs, the spine remains tall, and the eyes look straight ahead.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright with spine tall and neutral, head positioned centrally with eyes looking straight ahead, both hands clasped firmly behind the head at the base of the skull with elbows spread wide to the sides. The neck extensors appear visibly engaged and tense as the head pushes isometrically backward into the clasped hands, creating visible muscular tension in the posterior neck and upper trapezius without any forward or backward head movement.

exercises.name: Isometric Cervical Flexion
exercises.pose_description: Standing or seated upright with one hand placed on the forehead. The head pushes forward into the hand with sustained effort while the hand resists the movement, creating an isometric contraction of the deep neck flexors. No visible movement occurs, the spine remains tall, and the chin stays level.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright with their spine tall and chin level, their right hand (or left, depending on variation) pressed firmly against their forehead with the elbow bent at approximately 90 degrees, while their head pushes isometrically forward into the resisting hand creating visible tension in the anterior neck without any actual head movement. The opposite arm hangs naturally at the side, and the engaged deep neck flexor muscles appear taut along the front and sides of the neck.

exercises.name: Isometric Quad Contraction
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with a small rolled towel or bolster placed under one knee. The knee presses downward into the towel, tightening the quadriceps and lifting the heel slightly off the floor. The contraction is held isometrically, the ankle is dorsiflexed, and the opposite leg rests extended on the floor.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains supine on their back with the working leg's knee bent approximately 20-30 degrees, pressing firmly down into the towel beneath it while the heel lifts visibly off the floor; the foot is dorsifexed with toes pointing toward the shin, and the quadriceps muscle of the working leg appears visibly contracted and tightened. The opposite leg remains fully extended and relaxed on the floor, while the torso stays flat against the ground facing upward.

exercises.name: Isometric Shoulder Activation
exercises.pose_description: Stand with your arms at your sides and elbows bent to 90 degrees, forearms pointing forward. Place your other hand against the palm of your affected arm.
exercises.end_pose_description: Press your affected arm forward against the resistance of your other hand without allowing any movement. Hold the contraction for 5-10 seconds, then relax and repeat 10 times.

exercises.name: Isometric Shoulder External Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Standing next to a wall or doorframe with the elbow bent at 90 degrees and pinned against the side. The back of the wrist or hand presses outward into the wall or doorframe with sustained effort, as if trying to externally rotate the shoulder. No visible movement occurs — the contraction is purely isometric. The torso remains upright.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing perpendicular to the wall, with their right elbow bent at 90 degrees and pressed firmly against their ribcage, while their wrist and forearm are pressed outward against the wall in external rotation—the shoulder and rotator cuff muscles visibly tensed and engaged. The torso remains perfectly still and aligned vertically, with the opposite arm at rest, and the face looks straight ahead as sustained isometric tension is held through the shoulder external rotators.

exercises.name: Isometric Shoulder Internal Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Standing next to a wall or doorframe with the elbow bent at 90 degrees and pinned against the side. The palm or front of the wrist presses inward into the wall or doorframe with sustained effort, as if trying to internally rotate the shoulder. No visible movement occurs — the contraction is purely isometric. The torso remains upright.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing perpendicular to the wall, with their right elbow bent at 90 degrees and pressed firmly against their ribcage, while their forearm and palm are pressed inward against the wall with maximum isometric tension. The shoulder and chest muscles on the working side appear visibly contracted and engaged, with the torso remaining stable and squared, demonstrating sustained internal rotation force against the immovable surface.

exercises.name: Isometric Thumb Abduction Hold
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright with your hand relaxed on a table, thumb abducted away from your fingers at a 45-degree angle. A resistance band provides light pressure against your thumb.
exercises.end_pose_description: Maintain your thumb position by resisting the band's pull back toward your fingers without moving. Hold this static contraction for the prescribed duration.

exercises.name: IT Band Foam Roll Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Sit on the ground and position a foam roller under your right hip, with your right leg extended over the roller. Support yourself with your hands behind you.
exercises.end_pose_description: Roll your body weight forward and backward along the IT band from hip to just above the knee, pausing on tender points for 20-30 seconds.

exercises.name: IT Band Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with legs crossed, the back leg crossing behind the front leg. The body leans to the side of the front leg, pushing the hip of the back leg outward while reaching the arm overhead toward the opposite side. A stretch is felt along the outer thigh and hip of the back leg.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands with their right leg crossed behind their left leg, torso leaning distinctly to the left with the left arm stretched overhead and reaching diagonally across toward the right side, creating a pronounced lateral flexion curve from hip to fingertips. The right hip is pushed outward and back, the left knee maintains a slight bend, and the head follows the spinal curve while facing forward, with the outer right thigh and hip visibly lengthened.

exercises.name: Knee Flexion ROM
exercises.pose_description: Seated on the edge of a chair with the working foot on the floor. The heel slides backward under the chair, bending the knee as far as comfortably possible to increase range of motion. The opposite foot remains flat on the floor, and the hands may rest on the thighs or grip the chair seat for stability.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains seated upright on the chair edge with the working knee bent to approximately 90-100 degrees or greater, with the heel positioned far back underneath the chair. The quadriceps and hip flexors appear engaged and shortened, while the hamstrings and calf muscles are visibly stretched. The torso stays vertical and stable, facing forward, with the non-working leg extended or relaxed.

exercises.name: Knee-to-Chest Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with one knee pulled up toward the chest, both hands clasping below the kneecap or behind the thigh. The opposite leg remains extended flat on the floor. The lower back relaxes and rounds gently into the floor, and the head and shoulders remain on the ground.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies supine on their back with one knee bent at approximately 90 degrees and pulled maximally toward the chest, hands clasped firmly below the kneecap or around the back of the thigh, while the opposite leg remains fully extended and relaxed on the floor. The lower back is pressed into the floor with gentle rounding, the head and shoulders stay neutral on the ground, and the hamstrings and glutes of the bent-knee leg appear visibly engaged and stretched.

exercises.name: Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch with Band
exercises.pose_description: Kneel on one knee with the other foot planted in front, creating a 90-degree angle at both hips. A resistance band is looped around the back knee for gentle assistance.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently press your hips forward while using the band to support and deepen the hip flexor stretch on the kneeling side. Maintain an upright torso and avoid arching your lower back excessively.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown with Band
exercises.pose_description: Seated in a chair or on the floor with a resistance band anchored overhead. Both hands grip the band wider than shoulder-width with palms facing forward. The elbows pull downward and back, driving the band toward the upper chest while squeezing the shoulder blades together. The torso remains upright and the core stays engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is seated upright with elbows bent at approximately 90 degrees, positioned close to the ribcage with upper arms nearly vertical and forearms angled slightly forward. The resistance band is pulled down to upper chest level with both hands roughly shoulder-width apart, shoulder blades visibly retracted and depressed, creating prominent definition across the lats, rhomboids, and upper back. The torso remains perpendicular to the ground with chest slightly lifted, facing directly forward.

exercises.name: Lat Stretches
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright, the figure reaches one arm overhead and leans to the opposite side, creating a long stretch along the side of the torso from hip to fingertips. The other arm hangs naturally at the side. Feet are shoulder-width apart with a slight lateral bend in the torso.
exercises.end_pose_description: The figure stands upright with feet shoulder-width apart, one arm stretched fully overhead with the elbow straight, while the torso leans deeply to the opposite side creating a pronounced C-curve from the hip through the extended fingertips. The opposite arm hangs relaxed at the side, and the latissimus dorsi and oblique muscles along the stretched side appear lengthened and engaged, with the figure's gaze following the overhead arm.

exercises.name: Lateral Band Walks
exercises.pose_description: Standing in a quarter-squat position with a resistance band looped around the ankles or just above the knees. Feet are shoulder-width apart with knees bent and hips hinged slightly. Steps are taken laterally, leading with one foot and following with the other, maintaining constant tension on the band. The torso stays upright and the knees do not cave inward.
exercises.end_pose_description: The figure stands in a wide quarter-squat stance with one leg fully extended laterally while the other remains bent, creating maximum horizontal separation between the feet and maximum tension on the resistance band. The torso remains upright and centered, knees stay aligned over toes (no inward collapse), and the glutes, hip abductors, and quadriceps are visibly engaged and contracted as the stepping leg reaches its furthest lateral position. The person faces forward with shoulders level and square to the camera.

exercises.name: Lateral Lunge with Dumbbell
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet together holding a dumbbell at chest height with both hands. Maintain an upright torso and engaged core.
exercises.end_pose_description: Step your right foot out to the side, shifting your weight onto that leg and lowering into a deep lateral lunge. Keep your left leg straight and return to standing by pushing through your right heel.

exercises.name: Lateral Lunge with Reach
exercises.pose_description: The figure takes a wide step to one side, bending that knee while keeping the other leg straight. The torso leans slightly forward and the opposite arm reaches toward the bent knee foot. The straight leg inner thigh is stretched. Weight is on the bent leg with the foot flat on the ground.
exercises.end_pose_description: The figure is in a deep lateral lunge position with the torso upright or slightly forward-leaning, the bent knee (on the lunging side) flexed to approximately 90 degrees with foot flat on the ground, while the opposite leg remains fully extended and straight behind or to the side. The arm on the side opposite the bent knee extends forward and across the body toward or past the bent knee's foot, with the shoulder rotated inward, while the torso shows visible engagement through the obliques and lateral core. The head faces forward in the direction of travel, and the weight is centered over the bent leg.

exercises.name: Lateral Side-Lying Clam Shell
exercises.target_area: Gluteus medius, hip external rotators, trochanteric bursa
exercises.pose_description: Lying on one side with hips bent to approximately 45 degrees and knees bent to 90 degrees, feet stacked together. The bottom arm extends under the head, and the top hand rests on the hip. The top knee opens upward like a clamshell while the feet stay together and the pelvis remains stable without rolling backward. A resistance band may be placed just above the knees.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies on their side with the top knee opened maximally upward (approximately 70-90 degrees), creating a wide angle between the two knees while the feet remain pressed together and the pelvis stays stable without rotating backward. The hip and glute muscles on the upper side are visibly engaged and contracted, while the lower body maintains its 45-degree hip bend and 90-degree knee bend position.

exercises.name: Lateral Step-Ups
exercises.pose_description: Begin by standing tall beside a low step or platform, with the working leg positioned closest to the step. Place the entire sole of the working foot flat onto the center of the step, keeping the non-working foot on the floor beside it, with your body facing forward and shoulders square.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands fully upright on top of the step with their body weight centered over the stepping leg, which is straight and engaged. The opposite leg hangs naturally off the step with a slight bend at the knee, while the torso remains tall and perpendicular to the ground with shoulders level and stable. The quadriceps, glutes, and calf of the weight-bearing leg are visibly contracted and engaged.

exercises.name: Levator Scapulae Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Standing or seated upright. The head rotates approximately 45 degrees to one side, then the chin tucks downward toward the armpit, looking diagonally down. The hand on the same side as the rotation gently assists by pulling the head further into the stretch. The opposite shoulder remains depressed, and a stretch is felt along the back of the neck on the opposite side.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright with their head rotated approximately 45 degrees to one side and chin tucked downward toward the same-side armpit, creating a diagonal downward gaze. The hand on the rotated side grasps or gently pulls the head, with the elbow bent and positioned near the chest, while the opposite shoulder is actively depressed downward. The posterior neck muscles on the non-rotated side appear visibly elongated and engaged in the stretch.

exercises.name: Long Arc Quads
exercises.pose_description: Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and hips flexed to 90 degrees, so your shins are parallel to the floor. Your arms should rest relaxed by your sides.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains supine or seated with their torso stable and upright, while the exercised leg is fully extended and horizontal to the ground with the knee completely straight (0 degrees flexion). The quadriceps muscles are visibly contracted and taut along the front of the thigh, creating a defined ridge from hip to knee, while the opposite leg remains in the starting position with knee bent at 90 degrees.

exercises.name: Lower Back Release Roll
exercises.pose_description: Lying on back with a foam roller positioned horizontally under the lower back just above the pelvis. Knees are bent with feet flat on the floor. The body gently rolls the foam roller up and down over the lumbar muscles by bending and straightening the legs, applying moderate pressure. Hands may be behind the head or crossed on the chest.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies on their back with knees fully bent and feet flat on the floor, positioned close to the glutes, while the foam roller is rolled to its highest point under the lower back, creating maximum lumbar extension and arch in the spine. The lower back muscles appear stretched and engaged as the body weight presses into the roller, with hands either supporting behind the head or resting on the chest, and the gaze directed upward toward the ceiling.

exercises.name: Lumbar Rotation Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with both knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Both knees drop together to one side toward the floor while the shoulders and upper back remain flat on the ground. The arms are extended out to the sides in a T position for stability. The head may turn to look toward the opposite side of the knees.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies supine with their torso flat against the ground while both knees are dropped maximally toward the floor on one side, creating a 45-60 degree angle at the hips. Their shoulders remain pressed flat on the ground perpendicular to their lower body, with arms extended outward in a T-position, and their head is turned to face the opposite direction of the dropped knees. The oblique and rotational muscles along the torso appear stretched and elongated across the twist created between the upper and lower body.

exercises.name: Lying Figure Four Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with both knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Cross one ankle over the opposite knee to form a figure-four shape.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently pull the uncrossed thigh toward your chest, feeling a stretch in the hip and glute of the crossed leg. Hold the stretch while maintaining a neutral spine and relaxed breathing.

exercises.name: Lying Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Lying on back at the edge of a bed or table with both knees pulled to the chest. One knee remains hugged to the chest while the other leg lowers off the edge, hanging down toward the floor with the knee slightly bent. Gravity pulls the lowered thigh into extension, stretching the hip flexors and front of the thigh. The lower back stays flat on the surface.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies supine on their back with their torso flat against the bed/table surface. One leg is pulled toward the chest with the knee bent at approximately 90 degrees, while the opposite leg hangs off the edge of the surface with a slightly bent knee, creating a deep stretch through the extended hip and anterior thigh. The lower back remains in contact with the surface, and the stretched leg's thigh is in full extension with the knee maintaining a gentle bend.

exercises.name: Marble Pickup
exercises.pose_description: Seated in a chair with one foot bare and marbles or small objects scattered on the floor. The toes grip and pick up individual marbles, transferring them to a cup or different location. The heel remains on the floor, and the foot flexors work to curl the toes around each marble.
exercises.end_pose_description: The seated person's bare foot is lifted slightly off the floor with toes fully curled and flexed around a marble, holding it suspended above the ground before depositing it into the cup. The calf and foot muscles are visibly contracted and engaged, with the toes forming a tight grip, while the heel remains anchored to the floor and the knee maintains a slight bend at approximately 90 degrees. The person faces forward in an upright seated posture with their torso stable against the chair back.

exercises.name: Median Nerve Glide
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with the affected arm extended out to the side at shoulder height. Starting with the wrist flexed and fingers curled toward the palm, the wrist gradually extends and the fingers straighten while the head tilts away from the outstretched arm. The movement alternates fluidly between the tensioned and relaxed positions to glide the median nerve.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright with the affected arm extended fully straight out to the side at shoulder height, wrist fully extended backward and fingers spread open and straightened. The head is tilted away from the outstretched arm, creating a visible diagonal line of tension from the fingertips through the torso. The chest faces forward while the extended arm remains perpendicular to the body, with visible engagement through the forearm and shoulder stabilizers.

exercises.name: Median Nerve Gliding
exercises.pose_description: Sit with your right arm at your side, elbow bent 90 degrees, palm facing inward. Keep your shoulder relaxed and your neck neutral.
exercises.end_pose_description: Sequentially straighten your elbow, rotate your palm outward, extend your wrist, and gently lean your head away. This mobilizes the median nerve through its entire pathway.

exercises.name: Mini Squats
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with feet shoulder-width apart. The hips push back and the knees bend to approximately 30 to 45 degrees in a partial squat, as if beginning to sit in a tall chair. Arms extend forward for counterbalance, the chest stays lifted, and the knees track over the toes without caving inward.
exercises.end_pose_description: The camera captures a person in a partial squat position with knees bent to approximately 30-45 degrees, hips pushed back, torso upright with chest lifted, and arms extended forward at shoulder height for balance. The quadriceps, glutes, and core muscles are visibly engaged and tensed, with the knees tracking directly over the toes and the back maintaining a neutral spine angle relative to the ground.

exercises.name: Modified Superman Hold
exercises.pose_description: Lie face down on the floor with your forehead resting on a rolled towel and arms at your sides. Keep your legs straight and relaxed on the ground.
exercises.end_pose_description: Lift your chest off the floor slightly by engaging your back extensors, keeping your gaze downward to maintain neutral cervical spine. Hold for 2-3 seconds without lifting your legs.

exercises.name: Monster Walks
exercises.pose_description: Standing in a quarter-squat position with a resistance band looped around the ankles or just above the knees. Feet are shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and the torso is slightly hinged forward at the hips. Steps are taken diagonally forward and outward, maintaining tension on the band throughout, like a monster walking.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands with one leg extended diagonally forward and outward at approximately 45 degrees, knee slightly bent, while the opposite leg remains planted with a bent knee in a quarter-squat position, maintaining forward hip hinge. The resistance band is visibly taut between the legs, and the glutes, outer hip, and thigh muscles are prominently engaged and contracted on the extended leg side, with the torso remaining upright and stable.

exercises.name: Neck Flexor Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright with good posture and shoulders relaxed. Head is in neutral position.
exercises.end_pose_description: Slowly lower your chin toward your chest, feeling a gentle stretch at the back of your neck and upper shoulders. Hold 20-30 seconds without forcing.

exercises.name: Neck Rotations
exercises.pose_description: Stand tall with the feet hip-width apart and arms relaxed at the sides. Keep the shoulders level and relaxed, with the head held in a neutral position, gazing straight forward.
exercises.end_pose_description: The head is rotated maximally to one side with the chin nearly touching or pointing toward the shoulder, while the torso remains perfectly still and upright facing forward. The neck muscles on the opposite side appear stretched and elongated, while the rotated side shows subtle engagement. The shoulders stay level and relaxed without any elevation or forward movement.

exercises.name: Neck Side Bends
exercises.pose_description: Standing or seated upright with the spine tall and shoulders relaxed. The head tilts to one side, bringing the ear toward the shoulder while the opposite shoulder remains depressed. One hand may gently assist the stretch by resting on top of the head. The face continues to point straight ahead without rotation.
exercises.end_pose_description: The head is maximally tilted toward one shoulder with the ear positioned as close as possible to the shoulder, while the opposite shoulder remains actively depressed and pulled downward, creating a visible stretch along the lateral neck and upper trapezius. The spine remains upright and tall with no rotation, the face points straight ahead, and one hand rests gently on top of the head applying light downward pressure, with the other arm relaxed at the side. The person maintains an upright standing posture with shoulders level relative to the hips, though the stretched side of the neck visibly lengthens.

exercises.name: Open Book Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Lying on one side with hips and knees bent to approximately 90 degrees stacked on top of each other. Both arms start extended in front at shoulder height, palms together. The top arm opens upward and rotates across the body like a book opening, reaching toward the floor on the opposite side while the knees remain stacked. The gaze follows the moving hand, creating a deep thoracic rotation.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies on their side with hips and knees stacked at 90-degree angles, while their top arm extends fully open across their body with the palm facing upward, reaching toward the floor behind them in a wide arc. Their torso is rotated toward the ceiling with their chest and shoulders opening maximally, their head turned to follow the extended arm, creating a visible stretch across the chest, shoulders, and upper back. Their lower body remains perfectly still and stacked, anchoring the stretch while the obliques and serratus anterior appear engaged to control the rotation.

exercises.name: Overhead Tricep Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with one arm raised overhead and the elbow bent, dropping the hand behind the head and between the shoulder blades. The opposite hand gently pushes the elbow further behind the head, deepening the stretch along the back of the upper arm. The torso remains tall and the head stays in a neutral position.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with their torso tall and shoulders level. One arm is raised overhead with the elbow bent at approximately 90 degrees, the hand dropped behind the head toward the upper back, while the opposite arm is bent and positioned to gently press the raised elbow further back, creating visible tension through the triceps and posterior shoulder. The head remains neutral, aligned with the spine, and the person's gaze is directed straight ahead.

exercises.name: Pallof Press
exercises.target_area: Obliques, transverse abdominis, anti-rotation core stability
exercises.pose_description: Standing perpendicular to a cable machine or band anchor point with feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent. Both hands hold the handle or band at the center of the chest. The arms press straight forward, extending fully, resisting the rotational pull of the band. The core is fully braced, the hips remain square, and the torso does not rotate.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands perpendicular to the cable machine with both arms fully extended straight forward at chest height, creating a 90-degree angle between the torso and extended arms. The core appears braced and rigid with the torso facing forward, shoulders square, and hips locked in place without any visible rotation despite the cable tension pulling laterally. The obliques and rectus abdominis are visibly engaged and tightened, resisting the rotational force.

exercises.name: Patellar Tendon Stretches
exercises.pose_description: Kneel on a soft mat with your toes tucked under and hips positioned over your knees. Place hands on the floor in front of you for light support.
exercises.end_pose_description: Slowly shift your hips backward and downward, feeling a stretch along the front of the shin and patellar tendon. Hold the stretch without forcing excessive tension.

exercises.name: Pec Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Standing beside a doorframe or wall. One arm is placed against the surface with the elbow bent at 90 degrees at shoulder height. The body rotates away from the anchored arm, opening the chest until a stretch is felt across the pectoral muscle and front of the shoulder. The feet are staggered for stability.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands in a staggered stance facing away from a doorframe, with their torso rotated open to approximately 45 degrees. Their anchored arm remains bent at 90 degrees against the frame at shoulder height, while their chest is visibly expanded and opened, with the pectoral muscles stretched taut across the front of the shoulder and chest. The head is turned slightly to follow the body rotation, creating a gentle twist through the spine.

exercises.name: Pectoralis Minor Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Stand facing a wall or doorway with one arm raised at shoulder height, elbow bent to 90 degrees. Place your forearm against the wall or doorframe.
exercises.end_pose_description: Step your body forward while keeping your forearm in place, feeling a stretch across your chest and front shoulder. Your chest opens up as you lean into the stretch.

exercises.name: Pelvic Tilts
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor hip-width apart. The lower back is gently pressed into the floor by engaging the abdominal muscles and tilting the pelvis posteriorly, flattening the natural lumbar curve. Arms rest at sides and shoulders remain relaxed on the floor.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains supine on their back with knees bent at approximately 90 degrees and feet flat on the floor, but the pelvis is maximally tilted posteriorly, causing the lower back to press firmly into the floor with no visible gap between the lumbar spine and the ground. The abdominal muscles are visibly engaged and contracted, the ribcage appears slightly depressed toward the pelvis, and the lower abdomen shows defined tension as the core is fully activated. The person faces directly upward with shoulders relaxed and arms at their sides.

exercises.name: Pendulum Circles
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and lean forward slightly, supporting your body with your uninvolved arm on a table or chair. Let your affected arm hang straight down toward the floor in a relaxed position.
exercises.end_pose_description: Using gentle momentum from your torso, swing your hanging arm in small circles, gradually increasing the circle size. Continue the circular motion smoothly for 30-60 seconds in both directions.

exercises.name: Pendulum Swings
exercises.pose_description: Standing with feet shoulder-width apart, bending forward at the waist approximately 45 to 60 degrees. The non-working arm rests on a table or chair for support. The affected arm hangs straight down like a pendulum and swings gently in small circles or back and forth, completely relaxed with no active muscle contraction.
exercises.end_pose_description: Standing next to a table with the left hand resting on it for support. The upper body is bent forward at the hips at about 45 degrees. The right arm hangs freely and has swung forward to the front of its arc, extended in front of the body.

exercises.name: Peroneal Tendon Glide with Band
exercises.pose_description: Sit with one leg extended and wrap a band around your foot at the base of the toes. Support your calf with your other hand for stability.
exercises.end_pose_description: Slowly plantarflex your foot (point toes away) while maintaining light band tension, promoting tendon mobility and reducing stiffness. Return to neutral and repeat.

exercises.name: Pigeon Pose
exercises.pose_description: Start on your hands and knees, facing forward. Position your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees directly under your hips, with your shins parallel to each other and your feet pointing straight back.
exercises.end_pose_description: Fold your torso forward over your bent leg, resting on your forearms or hands as tolerated. Keep your hips level and breathe deeply into the stretch without forcing deeper flexion.

exercises.name: Pigeon Pose Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Start on a mat in a modified hands-and-knees position. Your hands are under your shoulders, your right knee is bent and brought forward towards your right hand, with your right shin angled across your body and your right foot near your left hip. Your left leg is extended straight back behind you, with the top of your left foot on the mat.
exercises.end_pose_description: Lower your torso forward over your right leg, keeping your hips square to the ground. Hold this deep stretch feeling the external rotators and IT band lengthen.

exercises.name: Piriformis Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Sit on the floor with both knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Cross one ankle over the opposite knee, allowing the top knee to gently open outwards. Keep your back straight and hands resting on your shins or the floor behind you for support.
exercises.end_pose_description: The torso is folded forward at approximately 45-90 degrees toward the floor, with the chest approaching or nearly touching the crossed front leg, while the back leg extends behind in a kneeling position with hips squared forward. The arms are extended in front with hands planted on the floor for support, the head is neutral or slightly lowered, and the glutes and outer hip muscles of the front leg appear visibly stretched and engaged. The person's weight is distributed between the hands and knees, creating a deep forward fold that emphasizes the posterior chain and hip external rotators.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.pose_description: Body supported on forearms and toes in a straight line from head to heels. Elbows directly under shoulders, forearms flat on floor, core tight, hips level — not sagging or piking.
exercises.end_pose_description: The body forms a perfectly straight line from head to heels, held parallel to the ground with no sagging at the hips or pike at the shoulders. The forearms remain flat on the floor with elbows directly beneath the shoulders at 90-degree angles, while the core, glutes, and shoulder stabilizers appear visibly engaged and contracted. The person faces downward toward the floor with their neck neutral, shoulders packed down and back.

exercises.name: Plantar Fascia Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with one leg crossed over the opposite knee. Your foot is elevated and accessible for hand manipulation.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently pull your toes back toward your shin with your hand, feeling a stretch along the bottom of your foot. Maintain a gentle, sustained stretch without bouncing.

exercises.name: Plantar Fascia Stretch with Band
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with one leg extended in front of you or crossed over the opposite knee. Wrap a resistance band around the ball of your foot, holding both ends of the band in your hands.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently pull the band toward your body, flexing your toes back toward your shin while keeping your leg relatively straight. Hold the stretch feeling gentle tension along the bottom of your foot and arch.

exercises.name: Posterior Shoulder Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and your right arm crossed horizontally across your chest at shoulder height. Your right elbow should be slightly bent.
exercises.end_pose_description: Use your left hand to gently pull your right arm closer to your chest, stretching the back of your right shoulder. Keep your torso upright and avoid rotating your trunk during the stretch.

exercises.name: Posterior Shoulder Stretch with Band
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright, facing forward, with feet hip-width apart. Hold one end of a resistance band in your right hand and the other end in your left hand. Your right arm is extended across the front of your body at chest height, with a slight bend in the elbow, while your left hand holds the band near your left hip.
exercises.end_pose_description: Pull the band apart by moving your hands away from each other, opening your chest and squeezing your shoulder blades back. Your arms remain at chest height with the stretch felt across your chest and front shoulders.

exercises.name: Prayer Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Kneeling on the floor, sitting back on the heels with the torso folded forward and the chest resting on the thighs. Arms extend forward on the floor overhead with palms down, and the forehead rests on the floor. The hips stay pressed back toward the heels, creating a long stretch through the lower back, lats, and shoulders.
exercises.end_pose_description: The body forms a compressed forward fold with knees bent and glutes pressed firmly toward heels, while the torso is folded completely forward with the chest resting on the thighs and forehead touching the floor. The arms are fully extended overhead with palms flat on the floor, creating a long line from the fingertips through the spine, with shoulders internally rotated and rounded forward. The person faces downward toward the floor, with the back of the body creating a gentle arch from extended arms through the rounded spine to the compressed hip fold.

exercises.name: Pronation/Supination with Light Dumbbell
exercises.pose_description: Sit with your elbow bent at 90 degrees and tucked against your torso, holding a light dumbbell with a neutral grip (handshake position). Your forearm is parallel to the ground.
exercises.end_pose_description: Rotate your forearm to turn the palm upward (supination) or downward (pronation), moving only at the wrist and forearm. Return to neutral and repeat in the opposite direction.

exercises.name: Pronation and Supination with Light Weight
exercises.pose_description: Sit with your elbow bent 90 degrees and supported on a table, holding a light dumbbell (2-3 lbs) with a neutral grip. Your forearm is horizontal.
exercises.end_pose_description: Rotate your forearm so your palm faces down (pronation), then reverse to palm facing up (supination). Control the movement throughout the full range of motion.

exercises.name: Pronation and Supination Strengthening
exercises.pose_description: Sit with your elbow bent at 90 degrees, tucked against your body with your palm facing down. Imagine holding a hammer with your hand at a neutral position.
exercises.end_pose_description: Rotate your forearm to turn your palm upward, then rotate back to turn your palm downward in a slow, controlled twisting motion. Move only at the forearm and wrist, keeping your elbow fixed.

exercises.name: Prone Cobra
exercises.pose_description: Lie face down on the floor with your legs straight and the tops of your feet resting on the ground. Position your arms alongside your torso with your palms facing down and your head relaxed, looking towards the floor.
exercises.end_pose_description: Press through your forearms to lift your chest off the ground while keeping your pelvis and lower abdomen in contact with the floor. Hold the position while maintaining a neutral neck.

exercises.name: Prone Gastrocnemius Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Lie face down on a mat, supporting your upper body on your forearms with your elbows directly under your shoulders. Extend both legs straight back, keeping your knees fully extended and your feet in a neutral, relaxed position.
exercises.end_pose_description: Press the tops of your feet into the ground to stretch your calves, keeping your hips on the mat. Maintain the stretch position while breathing steadily.

exercises.name: Prone Glute Squeeze Holds
exercises.pose_description: Lying face down with legs extended straight and arms at sides or folded under the forehead. Both glute muscles are maximally squeezed together and held in a sustained isometric contraction. The legs remain on the floor, the hips press gently into the floor, and the contraction is held for several seconds before releasing.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains prone and motionless on the floor, face down with legs fully extended and straight behind them, arms positioned at sides or folded beneath the forehead. Both glute muscles are visibly tensed and contracted, creating a firm, rounded appearance in the buttocks region, while the hips maintain gentle contact with the floor and the entire lower body appears locked in rigid isometric tension.

exercises.name: Prone Hamstring Curl
exercises.pose_description: Lying face down with legs extended straight and arms folded under the chin. One heel curls toward the buttock by bending the knee against resistance from an ankle weight or band. The hips remain pressed into the floor, the thigh does not lift, and the movement is controlled in both the curling and lowering phases.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains prone (face down) with their torso flat against the ground and forehead resting on folded arms. The working leg's knee is maximally flexed (bent approximately 90 degrees or more), with the heel drawn close to the buttock, while the opposite leg remains fully extended. The hamstring of the bent leg appears visibly contracted and engaged, the hip stays pressed flat to the floor without lifting, and the person faces downward toward the ground.

exercises.name: Prone Hip Abduction
exercises.pose_description: Lie face-down on a bed or mat with a pillow under your hips for comfort and support. Keep your arms relaxed and your surgical leg extended straight.
exercises.end_pose_description: Lift your surgical leg out to the side, abducting at the hip while keeping your leg straight. Hold briefly at the top, then lower with control.

exercises.name: Prone Hip Adduction Lifts
exercises.pose_description: Lie face down with a resistance band looped around both legs above the knees. Rest your forehead on your hands and keep legs together initially.
exercises.end_pose_description: Squeeze your inner thighs together against the band while lifting both legs slightly off the ground. Hold the contraction before releasing.

exercises.name: Prone Hip Bridges
exercises.pose_description: Lie face down with forearms on the ground, elbows under shoulders, and legs extended with toes tucked under. Engage your core and glutes to stabilize your lower back.
exercises.end_pose_description: Drive your hips upward toward the ceiling, creating a straight line from head to knees while squeezing your glutes. Hold briefly at the top, then lower with control without fully relaxing your glutes.

exercises.name: Prone Hip Extension
exercises.pose_description: Lying face down with legs extended straight and arms folded under the chin or at sides. One leg lifts straight off the floor behind the body, squeezing the glute to drive the movement, while the knee remains straight. The hips and pelvis stay pressed into the floor, and the leg lifts to approximately 15 to 20 degrees.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains prone (face down) with their torso and head still pressed into the floor, while one leg is extended straight behind them at approximately 15-20 degrees of hip extension, creating a visible lift from the glute contraction. The extended leg maintains a straight knee with the foot pointed slightly downward, while the opposite leg remains flat on the floor and the pelvis stays firmly grounded. The glute of the working leg appears visibly contracted and engaged at the peak of the lift.

exercises.name: Prone Hip Extension Pulse
exercises.pose_description: Lying face down with legs extended straight and arms folded under the chin. One leg lifts a few inches off the floor with the knee straight, then performs small pulsing movements upward, rapidly contracting the glute at the top of each pulse. The hips remain pressed into the floor and the leg does not touch down between pulses.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies face-down on the floor with their forehead resting on folded arms, one leg extended straight and raised to its maximum height (approximately 8-12 inches off the ground) with the knee locked straight, while the opposite leg remains extended on the floor. The glute of the raised leg appears visibly contracted and engaged at the peak of the pulse, with the hips firmly planted against the floor and no rotation in the torso.

exercises.name: Prone Hip Internal Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Lie face down with your right leg bent at the knee with your foot positioned to the right side of your body. Your left leg remains extended, and your forehead rests on your hands.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently press your right knee toward the floor, rotating your hip internally to increase the stretch. Hold this position while maintaining a neutral spine and relaxed shoulders.

exercises.name: Prone Horizontal Abduction
exercises.pose_description: Lie face down on a bench with both arms hanging off the sides, elbows slightly bent with light dumbbells in hand. Your chest should be supported by the bench.
exercises.end_pose_description: Raise both arms out to the sides in a horizontal abduction, squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement. Lower the weights back down in a controlled manner.

exercises.name: Prone I-Y-T Raises
exercises.target_area: Rotator Cuff, Scapular Stabilizers & Lower Trapezius
exercises.pose_description: Lying face down on the floor or a bench with arms hanging down. The exercise cycles through three arm positions: I (arms lift straight overhead in line with the body), Y (arms lift at 45 degrees forming a Y shape), and T (arms lift straight out to the sides at 90 degrees). Thumbs point up, shoulder blades squeeze together, and the forehead stays on the floor.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies prone on the floor with their forehead resting down, shoulders fully retracted with prominent shoulder blade engagement visible along the upper back. Arms are lifted to shoulder height in one of three positions—either straight overhead in line with the body (I position), at 45-degree angles forming a Y shape, or extended directly out to the sides at 90 degrees (T position)—with elbows straight, thumbs pointing upward, and the entire upper back musculature visibly contracted and defined.

exercises.name: Prone I-Y-T Shoulder Activation
exercises.pose_description: Lying face down on the floor or an incline bench. The arms cycle through three positions with controlled holds: I (arms extended straight overhead close to the ears), Y (arms lifted at 45 degrees from the head), and T (arms lifted straight to the sides at 90 degrees). Thumbs point up, the shoulder blades squeeze together, and each position is held for a few seconds before transitioning.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies prone (face down) with their forehead resting on the mat, arms fully extended overhead at one of three positions: either straight up by the ears (I position), at 45-degree angles from the body (Y position), or directly out to the sides at 90 degrees (T position). The thumbs point upward, the shoulder blades are visibly squeezed and retracted toward the spine, and the upper back and rear deltoids appear engaged and lifted slightly off the ground.

exercises.name: Prone I-Y-T Holds
exercises.pose_description: Lie face down on a bench with your arms hanging toward the floor and your legs extended behind you. Your forehead rests on a small pad or folded towel.
exercises.end_pose_description: Raise your arms into I position (straight overhead), Y position (45 degrees), and T position (90 degrees out to sides), holding each position for 2-3 seconds with scapulae fully retracted.

exercises.name: Prone I-Y-T Shoulder Series with Band
exercises.pose_description: Lie face down on a bench or sturdy surface with feet on ground, holding light resistance band in both hands at shoulder height. Forehead rests on a small towel.
exercises.end_pose_description: Pull band outward and upward in an I position (arms overhead), then Y position (45 degrees), then T position (90 degrees), holding each briefly before returning. Perform 10-12 reps of each position.

exercises.name: Prone Knee Flexion
exercises.pose_description: Lying face down with legs extended straight and arms at sides or folded under the forehead. One knee bends, bringing the heel toward the buttock as far as comfortably possible. The hips remain pressed flat against the floor and the thigh of the bending leg does not lift off the surface.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies face-down on the ground with their torso and hips flat against the floor, head turned to one side or resting on folded arms. One knee is deeply flexed with the heel drawn up toward the buttock at approximately 90 degrees or greater knee bend, while the opposite leg remains fully extended. The quadriceps of the bent leg and the hamstrings appear visibly engaged and contracted as the heel approaches the glute.

exercises.name: Prone Lumbar Extension with Band
exercises.pose_description: Lie face down on the floor with your forearms on the ground, elbows under your shoulders. A resistance band is looped around your mid-back and anchored securely beneath you.
exercises.end_pose_description: Push through your forearms and gently lift your chest off the ground while the band provides resistance. Hold this extended position while maintaining a neutral spine and avoiding excessive arching.

exercises.name: Prone Press-Up
exercises.pose_description: Lying face down with hands positioned under the shoulders as if preparing for a push-up. The upper body presses upward by straightening the arms, lifting the chest off the floor while the hips and pelvis remain in contact with the floor. The lower back extends into a gentle arch, and the head looks forward. The arms may be fully or partially extended depending on comfort.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is viewed from the side, lying prone with arms fully or nearly fully extended, pressing the upper torso upward so the chest lifts several inches off the floor while the hips, pelvis, and thighs remain in contact with the ground. The lower back is noticeably arched, the head is held neutral or slightly extended looking forward, and the shoulders appear drawn back with visible engagement through the chest and anterior shoulders. The body forms a curved line from the extended arms through the arched spine to the grounded lower body.

exercises.name: Prone Scapular Retraction
exercises.pose_description: Lying face down with arms at sides, palms facing down toward the thighs. The shoulder blades squeeze firmly together and downward, lifting the chest slightly off the floor. The forehead may remain on the floor or lift slightly, and the arms lift a few inches off the ground as the scapulae retract. The lower body stays relaxed.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies prone with their chest lifted noticeably off the floor, shoulders pulled back and down with scapulae maximally retracted, creating visible tension across the upper back and between the shoulder blades. The arms are extended straight or nearly straight at the sides, lifted a few inches off the ground with palms facing down, while the head remains neutral or slightly lifted, and the lower body stays flat and relaxed against the floor.

exercises.name: Prone Shoulder Abduction (Dumbbell)
exercises.pose_description: Lie face down on a bench or inclined surface with your affected arm hanging down toward the floor. Hold a light dumbbell in your affected hand with your arm in a neutral position.
exercises.end_pose_description: Raise the dumbbell out to the side, lifting your arm to shoulder height in an abduction motion. Keep your elbow slightly bent and move slowly with control, avoiding momentum.

exercises.name: Prone Shoulder Extension with Band
exercises.pose_description: Lie face down on a table or bed with your arms hanging down toward the floor, holding a light resistance band in both hands. Your forehead rests on the table and your core is engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: Raise your arms out to your sides and slightly back, squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement. Your arms form a gentle arc and your chest stays on the table throughout.

exercises.name: Prone Shoulder External Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Lie face down on a flat bench with your affected arm hanging off the side, elbow bent at 90 degrees with a light dumbbell in hand. Your upper arm should be parallel to the ground.
exercises.end_pose_description: Rotate your forearm upward by externally rotating your shoulder, bringing the dumbbell toward the ceiling. Hold briefly at the top, then lower back to the starting position.

exercises.name: Prone Shoulder Flexion
exercises.pose_description: Lying face down with the forehead resting on the floor and arms extended overhead on the ground. One or both arms lift straight off the floor with thumbs pointing up, raising the arm as high as possible while keeping the forehead down and the rest of the body flat. The shoulder blade retracts and depresses as the arm lifts.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies prone (face down) with forehead remaining on the floor, one or both arms raised straight overhead at approximately 180 degrees of shoulder flexion, with thumbs pointing upward and arms fully extended. The shoulder blades are visibly retracted and depressed, creating prominent muscle definition across the upper back, rear shoulders, and lower trapezius, while the torso and lower body remain flat and stationary against the ground.

exercises.name: Prone Shoulder I-Y-T
exercises.pose_description: Lie face-down on a firm surface with a small pillow under your forehead to keep your neck neutral. Let both arms rest alongside your body with palms facing down.
exercises.end_pose_description: Lift both arms off the surface in sequence forming an 'I' (arms overhead), then a 'Y' (arms at 45 degrees), then a 'T' (arms out to sides). Return to starting position and repeat, holding each position for 1-2 seconds.

exercises.name: Prone Shoulder Squeeze on Pillow
exercises.pose_description: Lie face down on a bed or mat with a pillow under your chest for comfort, arms at your sides with elbows bent. Your forehead rests on a small towel roll to keep your neck neutral.
exercises.end_pose_description: Squeeze your shoulder blades together, lifting your arms slightly off the bed while maintaining the elbow bend. Hold the contraction for 2 seconds, focusing on activating the muscles between your shoulder blades.

exercises.name: Prone Shoulder Stability Ball Y-Raises
exercises.pose_description: Lie face down over a stability ball with your chest supported and your feet anchored on the floor. Your arms hang straight down with a light dumbbell in each hand.
exercises.end_pose_description: Raise both arms out to the sides and slightly forward in a 'Y' position to shoulder height, squeezing your shoulder blades together. Lower the dumbbells back down in a controlled manner.

exercises.name: Prone T Raises
exercises.pose_description: Lying face down on the floor or a bench with arms hanging down or resting on the floor. Both arms lift straight out to the sides at 90 degrees from the torso, forming a T shape, with thumbs pointing toward the ceiling. The shoulder blades squeeze firmly together and the arms lift to body height. The forehead rests on the floor.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies face-down with their body flat against the ground, arms extended directly out to the sides at 90 degrees from the torso in a perfect T-shape, with elbows straight and thumbs pointing upward toward the ceiling. The shoulder blades are pulled tightly together and the arms are lifted to approximately shoulder height, creating visible tension across the upper back and rear shoulders. The forehead remains resting on the floor while the chest and shoulders display prominent muscle engagement across the trapezius, rhomboids, and posterior deltoids.

exercises.name: Prone Thoracic Extension Hold
exercises.pose_description: Lie face down with your forehead resting on a folded towel and arms at your sides with palms facing up. Keep your legs extended and relaxed.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently lift your chest off the floor using your thoracic muscles while keeping your pelvis and legs on the ground. Hold briefly and return to starting position with controlled movement.

exercises.name: Prone Y Raises
exercises.pose_description: Lying face down on the floor or a bench with arms hanging down or resting on the floor. Both arms lift upward and outward at approximately 45 degrees from the head, forming a Y shape, with thumbs pointing toward the ceiling. The forehead rests on the floor, the shoulder blades squeeze together, and the arms lift to approximately ear height.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies prone (face down) on the floor with both arms extended upward and outward at approximately 45-degree angles from the body, forming a Y-shape with thumbs pointing toward the ceiling and arms at roughly ear height. The shoulder blades are visibly squeezed together, the upper back is engaged and slightly lifted, the forehead remains on the floor, and the core appears taut to maintain spinal stability.

exercises.name: Prone YTW Raises
exercises.pose_description: Lie face down on a stability ball, supporting your chest and allowing your shoulders to clear the edge. Extend your legs behind you with feet on the ground for stability. Let your arms hang freely toward the floor, palms facing each other.
exercises.end_pose_description: Raise your arms in a Y position (overhead), then T position (out to sides), then W position (elbows bent at 90 degrees), pausing briefly at each position before returning to start.

exercises.name: Quadriceps Activation with Towel Roll
exercises.pose_description: Lie on your back with a rolled towel under one knee and the other leg extended flat on the floor. Keep your arms at your sides.
exercises.end_pose_description: Tighten the quadriceps of the leg with the towel roll by pressing the back of your knee downward into the towel. Hold the contraction while keeping your leg straight.

exercises.name: Quad Sets
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with BOTH legs fully extended straight along the ground, a small rolled towel under one knee. The quadriceps on one leg is visibly flexed and tight. Arms resting at sides, toes pointing up.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains supine on their back with both legs fully extended; the working leg's quadriceps is maximally contracted and visibly hardened, with the knee held in full extension and the foot pointed upward, while the towel roll remains under the knee; the non-working leg stays relaxed and flat on the ground, and the arms remain at rest at the sides.

exercises.name: Quad Stretches
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart, using a wall or gym equipment for balance. Bring one heel toward your glutes.
exercises.end_pose_description: Hold your ankle and gently pull the heel further toward your buttocks, feeling a stretch across the front of the thigh. Maintain an upright posture without arching your lower back.

exercises.name: Quadriceps Sets (Isometric)
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright with one leg fully extended and locked straight, knee joint completely contracted with the quadriceps visibly tensed and hardened. The opposite leg remains slightly bent in a supporting position, with the torso upright and stable, facing forward with arms relaxed at the sides or slightly forward for balance.

exercises.name: Quadriceps Stretch with Band
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright and place a resistance band around one foot. Hold both ends of the band with your hands at chest height.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently pull the band to bring your heel toward your glutes, feeling a stretch along the front of the thigh. Keep your knees parallel and avoid arching your lower back.

exercises.name: Quadruped Alternating Arm Raise
exercises.pose_description: Start on your hands and knees with hands under shoulders and knees under hips, maintaining a neutral spine. Keep your core engaged and look down to maintain neck alignment.
exercises.end_pose_description: Slowly raise one arm forward to shoulder height while keeping your body stable and level. Return to starting position and alternate sides in a controlled manner.

exercises.name: Quadruped Band Row
exercises.pose_description: Begin on hands and knees with a resistance band looped around your hands, maintaining a neutral spine and engaged core. Your hands should be shoulder-width apart with the band slack.
exercises.end_pose_description: Row one hand back by pulling the band, retracting your shoulder blade while keeping your torso stable and level. Your elbow should track close to your ribcage as you pull.

exercises.name: Quadruped Bird-Dog with Band
exercises.pose_description: Start on hands and knees with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips. A resistance band is wrapped around one foot and held in your opposite hand.
exercises.end_pose_description: Extend your opposite arm forward and leg backward in line with your body while the band provides resistance. Maintain a level hips and neutral spine throughout the movement.

exercises.name: Quadruped Hip Circles
exercises.pose_description: Begin on hands and knees with a neutral spine, wrists under shoulders and knees under hips. Engage your core to maintain stability throughout the movement.
exercises.end_pose_description: Lift one knee slightly off the ground and make slow, controlled circles, moving through the hip joint's full range of motion. Complete the desired number of circles in both directions before switching legs.

exercises.name: Quadruped Hip Extension
exercises.pose_description: Start on your hands and knees with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips. Keep your spine neutral and core engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: Extend one leg backward and upward, lifting your knee away from the floor while keeping the hip level. Squeeze your glutes at the top before lowering back down.

exercises.name: Quadruped Hip Flexor March
exercises.target_area: Hip flexors, core stabilizers, lower back
exercises.pose_description: On hands and knees in tabletop position with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips. One knee lifts slightly off the floor, driving the thigh upward in a marching motion while the hands remain planted. The movement alternates legs in a slow marching pattern. The spine remains neutral, the hips stay level, and the core is braced to prevent shifting.
exercises.end_pose_description: The performer is in quadruped position with one thigh driven upward to approximately hip height, knee bent at roughly 90 degrees, while the opposite leg remains extended and planted on the ground. The torso remains parallel to the ground with a neutral spine, shoulders stacked over wrists, and the pelvis stays level and square without rotation—the abdominals appear visibly engaged and braced. The lifted knee hovers several inches above the floor while the supporting arm and leg create stable anchor points.

exercises.name: Quadruped Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Start on hands and knees with shoulders over wrists and hips over knees. Maintain a neutral spine position.
exercises.end_pose_description: Slide one leg backward while dropping the hip toward the floor, creating a lunge-like position. Keep your core engaged and feel the stretch along the front of the back hip.

exercises.name: Quadruped Opposite Arm and Leg Raise
exercises.pose_description: Begin on hands and knees with a neutral spine, ensuring shoulders are over wrists and hips are over knees. Brace your core to stabilize your lumbar spine.
exercises.end_pose_description: Simultaneously raise your right arm and left leg to shoulder and hip height respectively while maintaining a level spine. Hold for 2 seconds and return to start.

exercises.name: Quadruped Pelvic Tilts
exercises.pose_description: On hands and knees in tabletop position with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips. The pelvis tilts posteriorly by tucking the tailbone under and rounding the lower back slightly, then anteriorly by arching the lower back and tilting the tailbone upward. The movement is isolated to the lumbar spine and pelvis while the upper back and shoulders remain still.
exercises.end_pose_description: From a side profile view, the person is in quadruped position with arms vertical and legs at 90-degree angles. The lower back is maximally arched with the tailbone pointed upward, the pelvis tilted anteriorly, and the chest lifted slightly forward—the abdominal muscles appear relaxed while the lower back extensors and hip flexors are visibly engaged. The head maintains neutral alignment following the spine's natural curve, and the shoulders remain stable directly over the wrists.

exercises.name: Quadruped Rock Backs
exercises.pose_description: Start on hands and knees with a neutral spine and core engaged. Hands are directly under shoulders and knees under hips.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently shift your hips back toward your heels while maintaining neutral spine alignment. Return to the starting position in a controlled manner.

exercises.name: Quadruped Rocking
exercises.pose_description: On hands and knees in tabletop position with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips. The hips push backward toward the heels in a rocking motion, sitting back as far as comfortably possible while the hands remain on the floor. The spine stays neutral and the movement is slow and rhythmic, stretching the hips and lower back.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is seated back on their heels in a deep hip flexion position, with arms extended forward and straight, hands still planted on the floor, creating a long diagonal line from the extended arms through the neutral spine. The hips are maximally retracted toward the heels, knees remain bent at approximately 90 degrees, and the head stays neutral with the gaze directed downward, with visible lengthening through the lower back, lats, and shoulders.

exercises.name: Quadruped Scapular Push-Up Plus
exercises.pose_description: Begin on hands and knees with hands directly under shoulders and knees under hips, maintaining a neutral spine. Your core is engaged and shoulders are packed down.
exercises.end_pose_description: Protract your scapulae by pushing the floor away, allowing your mid-back to round slightly upward between your shoulder blades. Hold this protraction position briefly before returning to the starting position.

exercises.name: Quadruped Shoulder Blade Squeeze
exercises.pose_description: Start on hands and knees with shoulders directly over wrists and hips over knees. Keep your spine neutral and core engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: Retract your shoulder blades by squeezing them together and slightly depressing them. Maintain this contraction while keeping your arms stable and spine neutral.

exercises.name: Quadruped Shoulder Stability (Modified)
exercises.pose_description: Get on your hands and knees with your hands directly under your shoulders and knees under your hips. Keep your core engaged and spine neutral with your head aligned with your spine.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently shift your weight forward and backward while maintaining stability in your shoulders. This controlled movement builds dynamic stability without excessive load on the healing rotator cuff.

exercises.name: Quadruped Shoulder Stability Hold
exercises.pose_description: Position yourself on hands and knees with shoulders directly over wrists and hips over knees. Keep your spine neutral and core engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: Slowly lift one arm forward to shoulder height while maintaining stability through your supporting arm and torso. Hold for 2-3 seconds, then return and repeat on the opposite side.

exercises.name: Quadruped Shoulder Taps
exercises.pose_description: On hands and knees in tabletop position with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips, or in a high plank position. One hand lifts off the floor and taps the opposite shoulder, then returns to the ground. The movement alternates sides. The hips remain level without rocking side to side, and the core is braced to prevent rotation.
exercises.end_pose_description: One arm is bent at the elbow and crosses the body to tap the opposite shoulder, while the supporting arm remains straight and locked beneath the shoulder, with the body held in a rigid plank position parallel to the ground. The hips and shoulders remain level and square, showing strong engagement through the obliques and core stabilizers, with the torso resisting any rotation despite the asymmetrical arm position.

exercises.name: Quadruped Spinal Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Begin on your hands and knees with shoulders over wrists and hips over knees. Place your right hand behind your head with elbow pointing out.
exercises.end_pose_description: Rotate your torso to bring your right elbow toward your left knee, creating a gentle twist through your thoracic spine. Return to center and repeat on the opposite side.

exercises.name: Quadruped Thoracic Rotation
exercises.target_area: Intercostal muscles, thoracic spine, obliques, chest
exercises.pose_description: On hands and knees in tabletop position. One hand is placed behind the head with the elbow pointing out to the side. The torso rotates, driving the elbow toward the opposite hand on the floor (closing), then rotates upward, driving the elbow toward the ceiling (opening). The hips remain square over the knees and the rotation occurs through the thoracic spine.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is in quadruped position with the torso rotated maximally upward, the elbow that was behind the head now pointing toward the ceiling with the arm bent at approximately 90 degrees, while the gaze follows the elevated elbow. The opposite arm remains extended and planted on the floor, supporting the body weight, while the hips stay square and aligned over the knees with no rotation. The thoracic spine shows pronounced rotation and extension, with the ribcage visibly twisted open and the chest facing toward the elevated side.

exercises.name: Radial and Ulnar Deviation with Lightweight
exercises.pose_description: Sit with your forearm supported on a table, holding a light dumbbell in neutral grip with hand hanging off the edge. Keep your elbow stationary throughout.
exercises.end_pose_description: Gently move your wrist toward your thumb (radial deviation) and then toward your pinky (ulnar deviation). Control the movement with light weight to strengthen side-to-side stabilizers.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Ankle Eversion
exercises.pose_description: Standing or seated with a resistance band looped around the outside of the forefoot, anchored to a fixed point on the opposite side. The foot pushes outward against the band resistance, turning the sole of the foot away from the midline of the body. The lower leg remains stationary and the movement occurs purely at the ankle joint.
exercises.end_pose_description: The foot is maximally turned outward (everted), with the sole of the foot facing laterally away from the body's midline, while the knee remains straight and the lower leg stays stationary. The resistance band is fully stretched, pulling against the outer edge of the forefoot, and the lateral ankle and peroneal muscles along the outer shin appear visibly engaged and contracted.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Ankle Inversion
exercises.pose_description: Standing or seated with a resistance band looped around the inside of the forefoot, anchored to a fixed point on the same side. The foot pulls inward against the band resistance, turning the sole of the foot toward the midline of the body. The lower leg remains stationary and the movement occurs purely at the ankle joint.
exercises.end_pose_description: The foot is maximally inverted with the sole turned inward toward the body's midline, creating a pronounced angle at the ankle joint while the lower leg remains completely still and vertical. The resistance band is visibly taut and stretched, demonstrating full tension against the inward foot position. The tibialis anterior and other anterior tibial muscles appear contracted and defined along the front of the lower leg.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Dorsiflexion
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright with your affected leg extended or slightly bent. Loop a resistance band around the ball of your foot and hold both ends, with tension already in the band.
exercises.end_pose_description: Pull your toes toward your shin against the band resistance, flexing at the ankle while keeping your leg stable. Hold briefly, then slowly lower back to the starting position.

exercises.name: Resistance Band External Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a light resistance band in your affected hand. Your elbow is bent to 90 degrees and tucked against your ribcage with the band anchored to a fixed point at elbow height.
exercises.end_pose_description: Rotate your forearm outward against the band resistance, keeping your elbow stationary at your side. Return to the starting position in a controlled manner without allowing the band to snap back.

exercises.name: Resistance Band External Rotation at 90/90
exercises.target_area: Rotator Cuff (Infraspinatus & Teres Minor) & Shoulder Stability
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with the working arm abducted to 90 degrees and the elbow bent to 90 degrees, forming a goalpost position. A resistance band is anchored at elbow height. The forearm rotates upward from a position pointing down toward the floor to a position pointing toward the ceiling, externally rotating the shoulder while maintaining the 90/90 arm position. The elbow stays at shoulder height throughout.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with their working arm held at 90/90 position (shoulder abducted 90 degrees, elbow bent 90 degrees), and the forearm has externally rotated upward so it points toward the ceiling, creating a goalpost shape with the upper arm remaining parallel to the ground. The opposite arm hangs naturally at their side, and the torso remains stable and upright with visible engagement in the shoulder rotators and upper back musculature.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Hip Abduction
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with a resistance band looped around both thighs just above the knees. Maintain a slight bend in both knees and keep your chest upright.
exercises.end_pose_description: Step laterally to one side, keeping tension on the band throughout the movement. Return to center and repeat on the other side.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Hip Flexion
exercises.pose_description: Stand upright with a resistance band looped around one foot and holding the other end in both hands at waist height. Keep your standing leg straight with a slight knee bend.
exercises.end_pose_description: Pull your foot upward against the band resistance, lifting your knee toward your chest in a controlled motion. Maintain an upright posture and return slowly to the starting position.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Knee Extensions
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright in a chair with your back supported and both feet flat on the floor, knees bent at approximately 90 degrees. Loop a resistance band around the ankle of one leg and anchor the other end securely to a stable object positioned behind that foot, creating slight tension.
exercises.end_pose_description: Straighten your leg against the band resistance, extending the knee fully. Slowly return to the starting position with control.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Lateral Walks
exercises.pose_description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and place a resistance band around your thighs just above the knees. Maintain a slight bend in your knees and a neutral spine.
exercises.end_pose_description: Step sideways, maintaining tension in the band and keeping your chest upright. Return to center and repeat in the opposite direction.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Plantarflexion
exercises.pose_description: Sit upright with your affected leg extended or slightly bent in front of you. Loop a resistance band around the ball of your foot and hold both ends with tension in the band.
exercises.end_pose_description: Press your foot downward and away from your body against the band resistance, pointing your toes. Hold briefly, then return slowly to the starting position with control.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Pull-Apart
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with arms extended straight in front at shoulder height, holding a resistance band with both hands about shoulder-width apart. The hands pull the band apart horizontally by squeezing the shoulder blades together, stretching the band across the chest until the arms are out to the sides. The elbows remain straight throughout.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with both arms extended straight out to the sides at shoulder height, forming a T-shape with the body, while holding a stretched resistance band with elbows locked in full extension. The shoulder blades are visibly retracted and squeezed together, creating prominent definition across the upper back and rear deltoids, with the chest lifted and shoulders drawn back.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Shoulder External Rotation
